221	## Detailed Design
222	
223	### Core Rules
224	
225	Rules are grouped by topic (A-H); ids are stable, not sequential within a group (CT-42 to CT-44 sit with the topic they belong to). Rule ids are `CT-n`; formulas are `D.n` (Formulas); acceptance criteria `AC-CT-n` (Acceptance Criteria) and open questions `OQ-CT-n` (Open Questions). Each rule is stated as **Rule**, **Why**, **Source**. Where two specialist proposals differed and no earlier ruling decided it, the choice is marked "(orchestrator ruling: ...)". Names that Web Map & Transit marks provisional (`web.view`, `web.state`, `transit_state`) are used with that mark carried (WM-36). `HOME_ID` := the `derelict_id` of the `web.view.nodes[]` entry whose `kind` is the home ship (the WM-3 roster `kind`); it is a derived label, never a constant and never registered (WM defines no such constant). Godot-specific mechanisms are not designed here: each is marked "-> ADR candidate" (ADRs (a)-(f) are listed at the end of the section), and anything the engine reference cannot source is marked NOT SOURCEABLE. **Engine reference coverage:** `docs/engine-reference/godot/` has `modules/ui.md`, `modules/input.md`, `modules/rendering.md`, `VERSION.md` and `breaking-changes.md`; there is **no** `scripting.md` or `core.md`, and nothing on `ConfigFile`, `SceneTree.paused` / `process_mode`, `Window` display-mode APIs, `Input.mouse_mode`, key-echo detection, focus-out notifications, font-importer flags or AccessKit property names; those are NOT SOURCEABLE and are routed to the ADRs below.
226	
227	#### A. What the layer is
228	
229	**CT-1. A meta layer, not a place.**
230	*Rule.* The chart table is one PIPE layer-3 `CanvasLayer` in the **root viewport**, opened by the `chart_table` input action (Esc / Start) from the `gameplay` or `inspect_card` context (PCI:62: pause is reachable from both; in the pod, on a derelict, in the home-ship). It has no prop, no location, no lighting, no glow, no ambient, no occlusion and no camera jolt. It is scaled by the HUD scale `H` for the bitmap face and continuously for the reading face (PR-12).
231	*Why.* A prop would be a lit, lie-capable instrument (ART 7.0 row 1) and could lie; the meta layer is honest by definition (ART 7.0 row 3: "can a reading lie? never"). The chart must be reachable on a sortie, which a home-ship console could not be. An in-world "chart-table console" or ship schematic does not exist (IW-28, C4).
232	*Source.* PIPE:94-103 (PR-3); PCI:78; ART 7.0.
233	
234	**CT-2. Truth channel.**
235	*Rule.* Layer 3 is never wrapped by the Perception Filter or by Sanity. No gleam, glide, tremor or settle occurs on any chart, panel or menu element (ART 7.3: the three motion signatures are readings only, and nothing on this layer is a reading). The layer is pixel-identical at sanity stage 0 and at forced stage 3, apart from the world visible beneath the panel. It never carries Violet or Flesh (ART 4.6), and Alarm Red appears on no element, because the layer draws no failing instrument (HR-4: red is never text). The only motion on the layer is the filament drift (CT-13, CT-40), the ART 7.3 cut/fade band and the ART 7.3 bracket ease-out, and the linear hold bar (CT-22).
236	*Why.* P1; ART HR-6 names menu, pause and settings layers as anchors; PF:223 (row 9, TRUTH: the pass sits below every `CanvasLayer`); SN:1226 (TRUTH anchor).
237	*Source.* PIPE PR-3 / PR-10; ART 7.3, 7.4, HR-4, HR-6. **Note.** The world frozen or running under the panel keeps whatever it showed, including a lie (CT-4, Player Fantasy "Under hallucination"); the panel does not.
238	
239	**CT-3. Surface architecture: panel first, stable order.**
240	*Rule.* `chart_table` opens the **panel**, a right-third plate over the world (ART 7.4). The panel has exactly four items in this fixed order: **Resume, Chart, Display & Comfort, Save & Quit**. The order never changes with state. An item that cannot act is shown **disabled** (the disabled style of CT-VA-7: Hull Grey label and a dashed 1-px Hull Grey border, so it clears the 3:1 glyph floor by shape plus tone; it is no longer Graphite lit, which measured 2.8:1), never hidden *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Default focus on open is Resume (non-destructive). Chart (and any message plate) replaces the panel in a cut (a replacement is not an appearance, so it takes no fade), except under reduce flashing, where it uses the long end of the ART 7.3 fade band (`CHART_FADE_MS`, CT-13). A replacement that raises layer-3 coverage is a governed raise (the re-open governor below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. "Display & Comfort" opens its page inside the panel's column. The panel carries only item labels and the empty status-line slot that holds `FAILED` when a write fails (CT-17, *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*); every paragraph of copy lives on a full-bleed **message plate** on the chart-table register (CT-28).
241	*Why.* One entry point; the world stays visible under the panel as ART 7.4 specifies; the HUD (layer 2) stays visible and frozen behind the pause panel, except that an active warning mark is held ON solid (HUD HS-23; the HUD's rule, acknowledged here; the full-bleed chart covers layer 2 entirely); a stable order is a muscle-memory affordance and menu layers are anchors that must not shift (HR-6). The accepted cost is that the chart is two actions from a pause; CT-10 (a no-pick console press opens the chart) offsets it. A second `chart` action stays an Alpha playtest fallback owned by the Player Controller and is not designed here.
242	*Ruled (HR-13, ASK-CT-8, OQ-CT-15, OQ-CT-27): the re-open governor. A player-initiated toggle of a large plate counts toward the 3 Hz ceiling, and the layer and the kernel are rate-limited together, never the picture alone* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; creative-director ruling)*.
243	- **Coverage levels.** `c = 0` CLOSED; `c = 1` the panel family (`PANEL`, `SAVE_FAILED`, `DISPLAY_COMFORT` opened from the panel); `c = 2` any full-bleed in-session plate (`CHART`, `CHART_VIEW_ONLY`, `UI3_PLATE`). A **raise** is a transition that increases `c` (TX-13, TX-14, TX-16, TX-17, TX-18, TX-24, TX-25); a **lower** decreases it (TX-15, TX-19, TX-35). Boot-flow screens are not governed (no world is visible under them and they appear once per process).
244	- **Close and resume are never delayed.** Every lower takes effect on the press frame. In SOLO a close calls `request_resume` on that frame.
245	- **A raise that comes less than `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` after the most recent lower is queued** and applied the first presented frame at or after `t_last_lower + CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` on the layer's UI clock (CT-43). A raise with no lower in the preceding interval is applied at once (the first open after a quiet period is never delayed). A queued raise applies **as one unit**: the plate, the focus, and in SOLO the `request_pause` of a CLOSED-to-PANEL or CLOSED-to-CHART raise happen on the same frame, so the picture and the kernel state always match (a queued open leaves the layer CLOSED and the kernel `RUNNING`; it never leaves an opaque plate over a running sim, nor a paused sim with no plate).
246	- **The queue is latched, one slot, and cancellable.** The pressed intent is held even if the key is released before the interval ends; there is one slot (the latest desired raise replaces an earlier queued one); only a `cancel` press while a raise is queued **cancels** it (the layer stays at its current level and a CLOSED layer is never opened and never paused) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: **a repeat `chart_table` press while a raise is queued is idempotent** (the raise stays queued, the latch is unchanged, nothing else happens), because at the first-launch default the lag is 1,000 ms and a player who pauses within a second of resuming (Moment 2, an emergency action) presses Esc twice from impatience and must not end up unpaused. **Queued acknowledgement:** the queue gives an audio-only acknowledgement (a single cue, no visual element, so no flash risk) requested from Adaptive Audio (ASK-CT-20; the layer plays no sound itself, CT-29): the cue is `UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED` (semantics in CT-29, test in AC-CT-138); until Audio ships its asset the queued press stays the "documented reason" of CT-GF-2(1) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G2/G6: CT-3 queued acknowledgement, ASK-CT-20)*. **Panel item state while a raise is queued from the panel** (Chart accepted, or Save & Quit refused into `UI3_PLATE`, within the interval of the last lower): the panel stays shown unchanged, all four items stay enabled, the bracket stays on the accepted item, and a repeat accept is idempotent; `cancel` cancels the queued raise first (the panel stays), and a second `cancel` closes the panel. The queue is cleared by any `request_restore` (TX-27). A queued raise has no hold or fill running, so nothing destructive is pending.
247	- **Scope.** The governor applies to the panel open (TX-13), the console-press chart open (TX-18; this supersedes the earlier "never to the console-press entry"), Chart from the panel (TX-16, TX-17) and the message-plate raises (TX-24, TX-25). It never delays the irreversible console press itself: a console press with a valid pick submits `pod_hop` at once and is not a layer raise (CT-10).
248	- **Value and derivation.** `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` = `ceil(1000 / FLASH_MAX_PER_S)` = 334 ms (registry `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3, locked; same derivation as the registry's 334 ms floor for lying-readout ticks). With raises at least that far from the preceding lower, a rolling 1-s window holds at most three raises and so at most six opposing layer transitions, which scores `F <= 3` under the registry `flash_count` (Pipeline PR-13, D.15: `F = ceil(n_transitions / 2)`). **Under reduce flashing** the interval is `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS_REDUCED` = 1000 ms (`[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 500-1500), so at most one raise per rolling second and `F <= 2`; with the long end of the fade band this is the toggle's real work. **Because reduce flashing is ON at first launch (user ruling D79, CT-19), 1000 ms is the interval every new player meets until they turn the toggle off**; the 334 ms interval is what a player who opts out, or a returning player who switched it off, gets. 335	**The home-ship composite (the drawing rule for berthed and absorbed records)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. `chart_layout.json` (CT-12) carries, per derelict record, a `home_attach` offset `(dx, dy)` in chart-local art px from HOME's centre to the record's centre, authored so the 24x24 glyph rectangles **share one full edge** (`|dx| = 24, dy = 0` or `dx = 0, |dy| = 24`); "the socket edge" of WM:1083 is that shared edge. The composite is drawn from the existing glyph assets, with no new asset: (a) **berthed**: the record's template glyph at the attach point plus the A17 seam quad on the shared edge; the record is **not** drawn at its authored position while berthed, and returns there on `unberth`; (b) **ABSORBED**: the same glyph at the same attach point in the HOME stroke style, with the seam replaced by the Ground erase quad; (c) the pod marker follows the drawn position of its record. **Berthed and absorbed records are excluded from the snap graph, from focus and from the pairwise `S_MIN` lint of their authored positions**, because they are not focusable; their attach rectangles are linted instead: each must not overlap any other node's bracket-padded rectangle, and HOME plus every attach rectangle must lie inside the chart frame (D.1b). The lint is re-run for each composite state of AC-CT-120: none, B berthed, B absorbed, A and B absorbed. If two records are given the same side of HOME the lint fails the build. Status is read from `web.view` on every change; a record whose status leaves ABSORBED or `berthed` (an `unberth`, or a restore) is simply drawn at its authored position again.
336	
337	**Per-state paint table for the composite** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (Moment 4's only visible reward for the berth-and-weld loop, so "HOME stroke style" is defined here). Every glyph is painted in four layers, back to front: the Ground clearing (`NODE_CLEAR_PAD_PX`), the **interior fill**, the **silhouette stroke**, the **outline**; the seam and erase quads come last.
338	
339	| State | Interior fill | Silhouette stroke | Outline | Last quad |
340	|---|---|---|---|---|
341	| HOME | Ground | Graphite lit, 1 px (HOME's own stroke, the reference for "HOME stroke style") | 1-px Hull Grey | the Tungsten point; no seam |
342	| UNSEEN | Ground | Graphite lit plain rectangle | 1-px Hull Grey | none |
343	| SEEN / BOARDED | Ground | Graphite lit, template silhouette | 1-px Hull Grey | the Tungsten tick if `unknown_seen` |
344	| `berthed` | Ground | Graphite lit, template silhouette, at the attach point | 1-px Hull Grey | solid 1-px **Hull Grey seam** quad on the shared edge (A17) |
345	| ABSORBED | Ground | **exactly HOME's stroke** (same colour and weight), at the attach point | 1-px Hull Grey | a **Ground erase quad** over every stroke and outline column of the shared edge (inset 1 art px at each end so the corners close); the erase repaints the **interior-fill colour (Ground)**, so the two interiors read as one and no seam is visible; no tick and no Tungsten point on the record |
346	| ORPHAN | Ground | Graphite mid | dashed 1-px Hull Grey | none |
347	
348	The fill and the erase colour are the same Ground, which is why the erase leaves no visible seam between two fills. The art-director signs the geometry of A1 to A3 and A17 (how many stroke and outline columns the shared edge carries) **before** any golden of AC-CT-120 is captured; the erase quad spans however many columns that geometry has.
349	State is never carried by colour alone: every state has a distinct silhouette or mark (tick, seam, detachment, glyph), satisfying SL:1010 and HR-10 by construction. Routes, seams and rule lines are 1-art-px quads aligned to whole art px, never width-1 line draws on a fractional transform (4.7 `CanvasItem` line drawing has no antialiasing feather; -> ADR candidate (b)).
350	*Visibility, ruled (art-director risks R-AD-4 and R-AD-5; OQ-CT-24 closed as "add outline")* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: Graphite lit on Ground measures 2.77:1, below the 3:1 glyph floor (HR-12), and ORPHAN's Graphite mid about 1.2:1. The glyph assets (A1 to A3 and the ORPHAN variant) therefore carry a **1-px Hull Grey outline** (about 5.3:1) on every UNSEEN, SEEN, BOARDED and HOME silhouette, and ORPHAN carries a **dashed 1-px Hull Grey outline** (dashed means severed: a shape, not a colour; selectability stays absent). This is a glyph change, not a change to the WM drawing rows (WM:1041-1046). Each node also sits on a **Ground clearing** (`NODE_CLEAR_PAD_PX` 3 art px, `[PLACEHOLDER]`, a Ground quad drawn above the filament sheet and below the glyph) so a decorative filament can never out-contrast a target. The contrast of every pair is a computed palette lint (AC-CT-75c), not an eyeballed claim. The asset names are WM's A10 set: the change is routed to WM and to the art-director as a cross-GDD note.
351	*Source.* WM:1036-1050; ART 3.4, 4.6, 7.2, 7.4.

353	**CT-12. Layout data is authored, per record.**
354	*Rule.* A Chart-Table-owned content file (`assets/data/ui/chart_layout.json`, path provisional) holds authored node positions **per record (`derelict_id`) in chart-local art px** inside the chart safe frame (D.1b), a **`home_attach` offset per derelict record** (the attach point at which a berthed or absorbed record is drawn against HOME, CT-11 "the home-ship composite"), the depth-ring radii, the filament texture reference and a stable per-record **ordinal**; the silhouette glyph is chosen **by `template_id`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Nothing is derived from `world_slot`, leg data, ticks or distance (WM:1049, ASK-AD-7); `world_slot` is in `web.view` and is never read for layout. A missing record position is a content-lint failure; at runtime a deterministic fallback slot on the outer ring is used and a log line is emitted. Positions are authored cosmetic placements and are lint-checked so no authored distance correlates with any Web Map & Transit cost value.
355	*Why.* Two derelicts of one template must not overlap; a derived layout is a distance read, and a distance read is a cost number by proxy.
356	*Layout coordinate space (closed by checkpoint ruling Q7; OQ-CT-11 is closed).* Positions are authored in art px inside a **fixed chart frame** `CHART_FRAME` 288 x 162 art px (`[PLACEHOLDER]`, derived from the smallest spatial canvas, D.1b) and drawn at an integer **chart multiplier** `m` applied to positions only (D.1b); glyphs stay 24x24 at `H`. The **compact layout** (CT-44) applies iff `m < 1`. The ui-programmer's normalised (u, v) coordinates were declined.
357	*Source.* WM:1049, ASK-AD-7 (WM:1180).
358	
359	**CT-13. Depth rings, filaments and the only motion.**
360	*Rule.* The chart field is drawn as concentric **ring bands** darkening toward the centre, ending in a centre disc that is exactly Void Steel `#0B1018`; `CHART_RING_STEPS` (3, `[PLACEHOLDER]`) counts the ring bands. All MVP nodes sit in ring 1, the outermost band, which is Ground `#1C2128` itself; rings 2 and 3 are the horizon, not content, and carry no node, label or tick (WM:1050). The darkening is an **ordering contract** (outer lightest, each step darker than the one outside it by at least `RING_STEP_MIN_CHANNEL` `[PLACEHOLDER]` per channel, centre disc darkest; ring 1 is Ground itself, the disc is Void Steel itself, and the tones between are the D.6 interpolation), not a percentage restated as a value: ART 7.4 and WM:1050 say "about 4 % darker", but the art-director found that reading cannot be satisfied together with "the inner ring reaches Void Steel" and stays near the visibility threshold (flag F-6; wording clarification routed to the art-bible owner; exact tones are derived values in D.6 and Visual/Audio, never new palette entries). `depth_label` and ring numbering carry no progress semantics (WM:1309). Filaments are Hull Grey, 1 art px, branching, non-repeating, no right angles (ART 3.4), **authored texture layers** (not procedural), drifting by whole-art-px offsets on the layer's own UI clock (CT-43) at no more than the ART 7.3 ceiling, stepped through an authored irregular interval table, floored at one second, so the step is never a metronome beat (D.5; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, G2: creative-director lean, authored irregular step table)*), **in ring 1 only**, and never under a node (every node sits on a Ground clearing, CT-11); the filaments of rings 2 and 3 are static and denser toward the centre. **Reduced motion** stops the drift and holds its current whole-pixel offset (no snap-back) and turns the bracket relocation into a cut; it does **not** turn fades into cuts (a fade is not spatial motion) *(orchestrator ruling: the art-director's reading, over the ux-designer's "fades become cuts")*. **Reduce flashing** (a separate toggle, PR-13(c)) uses the long end of the ART 7.3 fade band and forbids a hard cut of a large plate. The two toggles together are the union. Reduce flashing also lengthens the re-open interval of the governor (CT-3: 334 ms to 1000 ms), which is what reduces the flash *count*; the 100 to 120 ms fade change alone reduces the step steepness and not the count *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Everything human on the chart is static.
361	*Why.* The composition must pull inward (ART 2.11 carried element). `present_time` is frozen under pause (PIPE:265), so the drift cannot use it.
362	*Source.* ART 2.11, 3.4, 7.3, 7.4, HR-8; WM:1050; PIPE:265; PIPE PR-13(c).
363	
364	**CT-14. No label of any kind beside a node or the selection.**
365	*Rule.* No distance, travel time, fuel figure, danger rating, loot estimate, "recommended" marker, name or number sits beside any node or the selection, **except the CT-44 neutral ordinal in the compact layout, which is not a name** (a slot mark with no identity: it never varies with status, `template_id`, kind or depth, and UNSEEN and SEEN rows render the identical key form; AC-CT-112). The only text on the chart is the state word `IN TRANSIT` (CT-15), the layer's own control hints (keycap glyphs) and, in the compact layout only, those neutral ordinals. The spatial map carries no text beside any node, UNSEEN or SEEN.
366	*Why.* A distance invites "closer = cheaper", a cost number by proxy (P1; WM guard rail 7; OQ-WM-34 default: "No label is required; none is derived"). The art bible's selection row mentions "label and distance beside it"; that wording is superseded by this rule and routed as a clarification to the art-bible owner.
367	*Source.* WM:1049; OQ-WM-34.
368	
369	**CT-15. The chart while `transit_state != IDLE` (LEG, ARRIVING, BERTHING; the Pipeline's `TRANSIT_HOLD` included).**
370	*Rule.* The layer stays openable and is **view-only**. The pick is frozen (CT-8); nothing on the map is focusable or activatable; focus rests on the layer's Back hint (a text-labelled control). The state word `IN TRANSIT` (instrument face) is shown **iff `pod_at == IN_FLIGHT`**: a direct `web.view` read, no other condition. It sits at a **fixed position** inside the chamfered border at the top-left, anchored to the picture rect with the 5 % safe margin (PIPE:88), and is never placed near the origin node, the target node or along the route, because position would read as direction or progress that `web.view` structurally lacks. It appears and disappears in a cut with the data; no ellipsis animation, no dots, no blink. BERTHING shows **no** state word and no progress element (WM:1307: a berth is witnessed by the world). No pod marker is interpolated (WM:1048). **Nothing is drawn from `ChartPick` while non-IDLE**: the chart must never reconstruct the target from its own pick, because the pick resets on restore, is host-local and is wrong in co-op. The planned-sortie route in flight is drawn **only from `web.view.leg_target_id` and `leg_dir`** (WM-36; closes C12 and ASK-CT-3): on an OUT leg the dashed Tungsten line runs HOME to `leg_target_id`; on a BACK leg (`leg_target_id` is HOME, the origin is not published) no route is drawn and the `IN TRANSIT` word stands alone. The chart never calls `web.leg_timing()` (Audio-only, WM:300).
371	*Source.* WM:1048, :1268, :1307; WM-36; ASK-AD-7.
372	
373	**CT-16. Layout contract across every reachable canvas.**
374	*Rule.* The layer is asserted at every reachable HUD canvas `picture / H`, with `H` an integer in `[H_default, 2 * H_default]`, `H_default = max(k, 3)` and `k` the integer **world scale** (PIPE D.4; **zoom never changes the HUD canvas**, PR-12: "H is independent of k and of zoom"). The required canvas rows are: 1080p / 1440p / 2160p `keep` at `H_default`, 640 x 360; 1080p at `2 * H_default`, 320 x 180; Deck 1280x800 `expand` at H 3, 426.67 x 266.67, and at H 6, 213.33 x 133.33; 720p at H 3, 426.67 x 240, and at H 6, **213.33 x 120, the smallest reachable canvas**. Layout is anchor-relative only (PIPE:88, 5 % safe margin) and **every layer-3 rectangle is positioned by anchors 0 or 1 plus integer HUD-px offsets**; a centred element is permitted only if its on-screen width is an even number of screen pixels. The panel is therefore `floor(canvas_w / 3)` HUD px wide, hung from a right anchor of 1, so every edge is an integer screen pixel at every `H` and "a third" holds to within one screen pixel (orchestrator ruling: the ui-programmer's integer rule over the ux-designer's fractional `canvas_w / 3`; D.1 in Formulas). Where the chart multiplier `m` (D.1b) is below 1 the chart switches to the compact layout (CT-44). Nothing scrolls at MVP's node and item count. At MVP only `H_default` is player-reachable (HUD scale is Settings', Alpha), but the contract and its acceptance criteria cover the full range through a forced-`H` test hook.
375	*Why.* The reflexion log (2026-10-26, "invariant — inner box unsatisfiable at zoom-in fields"): an invariant written against the default must be re-checked whenever a later decision adds reachable states.

376	*Source.* PIPE PR-12 (PIPE:224), D.4 (PIPE:369-386); `docs/consistency-failures.md`.
377	
378	#### D. The panel, settings and the notice
379	
380	**CT-17. The pause panel's content.**
381	*Rule* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: Save/Load's UI-2 was amended the same day to "no save fact on the pause panel"; the newest-record line, the playtime of the newest generation, is on the main-menu Continue screen only, read on every `MAIN_MENU` entry (re-read after a FAULTED return, a failed `new_game` or a Display & Comfort return, TX-34, TX-37; never refreshed while the menu stays open) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, because pausing is free and a line that changed between writes would show that a write is overdue)*. The panel shows the four items of CT-3 and **no save fact**: no playtime, no depth label, no countdown, no "time since", no gate state, no per-write mark (SL UI-2, AC-SL-133). Its content is identical across any number of autosave periods. It reserves one **status-line slot** (height `PANEL_RECORD_LINE_H_HUD`, id retained for continuity, D.1) that is **empty** except in `SAVE_FAILED`, where it holds the plain word `FAILED` (CT-21); because the slot's presence is constant, opening the panel never reflows. The panel has **no title and no state word**: it never says "Paused" (in OVERLAY the sim is running, and a word that is false in one mode is a lie on the truth layer). `SaveInfo.depth_label` does **not** appear on the panel (it is on the main-menu Continue line only; the Web Map & Transit row at WM:1309 saying "pause panel / save list" is satisfied by the save list, routed as C13). Panel plate: opaque Ground (HR-2), one chamfered Graphite-lit border, one rivet mark per corner (ART 7.4). The world beneath is frozen exactly as lit, not dimmed, blurred or desaturated (PIPE:265); a click on that world does nothing (CT-41). Panel item labels are in the reading face (ART 7.1 assigns settings and long menu copy to the reading face; panel item labels follow it as menu copy, orchestrator ruling closing ASK-UP-3; a clarification row to the art-bible owner); the `FAILED` word and the Continue line's numerals are the instrument face.
382	*Source.* SL UI-2 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, UI-4; ART 7.4; PIPE:265; WM:1309.
383	
384	**CT-18. Display & Comfort page: exactly four controls.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
385	*Rule.* One page inside the panel's column (in-session) or the main menu's content column (boot-flow, from the Display & Comfort item of CT-23; the same S6, TX-36, TX-37) with four controls *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; master volume added 2026-10-27, user rulings)*: **display mode** (windowed / fullscreen / borderless), **reduced motion**, **reduce flashing** and **master volume**. Defaults *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: display mode and reduced motion are the pipeline hooks' defaults (PR-13; PIPE:301 "MVP exposes the hooks with defaults"); **reduce flashing is ON at first launch** (user ruling D79, OQ-CT-7, CT-19); master volume starts at its top step, which Adaptive Audio's master bus treats as unity (Adaptive Audio's call, CT-29). Display mode is a three-choice list whose current choice is marked by a shape plus a word (not colour alone); the two booleans are chamfered switches (ART 7.4) with an on/off **word**. **Master volume** *(Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), D85)*: a single row holding a **stepped control** of `VOLUME_STEPS` notches (10 at authoring, `[PLACEHOLDER]`; a stepped control and not a continuous slider so that a gamepad has exact steps, the same reason display mode is a list): Left / Right (the MenuInput directional feed, repeating by D.9) or a pointer click on a notch changes it by one step, the current step is marked by a shape plus a numeral (not colour alone), and step 0 is a legal choice (muted) shown with its numeral and no warning. The page publishes the step through the store's change signal; Adaptive Audio maps step to master-bus gain (the law, the floor and the default are its own; this layer carries no dB figure and plays no sound of its own, CT-29). It is not a safety toggle, so it is debounced like display mode (CT-19). Changes apply immediately and persist (CT-19); there is **no Apply button and no revert countdown** (a countdown would be a timer surface; any revert-on-failure safety is Settings' / an ADR). After a display-mode change the page reads back and shows the **applied** mode (a failed fullscreen request shows windowed); a mode change resizes the window, so `k`, `H_default`, the canvas and the panel width recompute live, the page stays open and focus is retained **by item id**, the bracket does not nudge and no animation plays on the relayout. The page carries only labels, switches and their words; it has no explanatory paragraphs. **Never on any page:** zoom (PIPE:232), rebinding, resolution list, world scale, **HUD scale** (deferred to Settings & Input Rebinding, Alpha: `H_default` already meets the 21-px floor on every display by construction), frame cap, V-sync, audio other than the one master volume control, the HR-15 ambient step (Lighting's), any true-value overlay (never an accessibility option, ART 7.4). Master volume is the fourth control (OQ-CT-1: Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): added at MVP, D85) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The page's height is re-derived in D.1c.
386	*Why.* The first three controls (display mode, reduced motion, reduce flashing) are those an outside playtester needs and that PR-13(c)/(e) makes load-bearing; each is a boolean or enum hook the pipeline already defines. Master volume is the fourth because Display & Comfort is now reachable from the main menu (CT-23), so a first-time player can open the page before any world exists and would otherwise find no audio control at all *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. `Window` display-mode behaviour and failure reporting are NOT SOURCEABLE in the engine reference.
387	*Source.* PIPE PR-13, PR-14 (PIPE:228, 232), PIPE:301; ART 7.4.

389	**CT-19. Settings store.**
390	*Rule.* The four comfort values (display mode, reduced motion, reduce flashing, master volume) and the `notice_seen` flag *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* live in a host-local, per-install `SettingsStore` seam: **not a kernel block, not a command, not WORLD or PROFILE scope** (PROFILE is per-campaign, SL-9; settings survive New campaign). Nothing in the simulation reads it (HR-6: "no game state may read or alter" anchors, PCI:845). Consumers (Lighting, the Filter, Audio, the Camera) read `reduced_motion` and `reduce_flashing` through the store's read interface and a presentation-only change signal. A missing or unreadable store is treated as first launch with the first-launch defaults (reduce flashing ON, reduced motion at the pipeline default, master volume at its top step) and the notice (CT-20) is shown again (the safe direction) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)* **The safety toggles (reduced motion, reduce flashing) and `notice_seen` are written synchronously on the change**, before the next presented frame, so a crash or a mashed-through notice never leaves a player who switched protection on unprotected; only display mode and master volume are debounced (`SETTINGS_WRITE_DEBOUNCE_MS` `[PLACEHOLDER]`, Tuning Knobs) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* and it is flushed on page close, on Save & Quit and on exit. A write failure keeps the values in memory and retries at the next flush; **when the store cannot be written the layer shows one plain ship-log line once per process** (the first failed write, `ct.*` key, placeholder copy "Settings could not be saved."), never again in that process, so a read-only store does not nag on every launch. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: placement, lifetime and fit.)* **Surface:** the line is one `LABEL_1` reading-face line in the **reserved settings-line slot** of the surface that is showing when the failure is detected: on S9 (the notice) under the dismiss item; on S6 (Display & Comfort) between the last control and the Back hint (the slot is always present and empty otherwise, so it never reflows the page, CT-17's invariant; D.1c and D.1d include it in the fit math at the spatial rows). If the failure is detected while neither surface is showing (a debounced flush on page close, on Save & Quit or on exit), the line is armed and drawn in the slot of the next S6 or S9 that opens, or in the panel's status-line slot (CT-17) if the panel is showing and `FAILED` is not, and is never drawn at exit. **Lifetime:** it stays until that surface closes, is then consumed and never returns in the process. At the compact rows (`m < 1`, DEFERRED-REACHABLE) the S6 slot is not reserved and the line is logged only (OQ-CT-40). A capture is owed (AC-CT-136). The few-hundred-byte write is on the UI thread and no thread is introduced. **First-launch default of reduce flashing is ON** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): the creative-director's recommendation (the safe direction: a crash or a mashed-through notice otherwise leaves the player who needed protection unprotected) is adopted (OQ-CT-7, D79; the Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline amends its PR-13 hook default to match). The ruling covers reduce flashing only; reduced motion keeps the pipeline's hook default. A fresh store therefore reads `reduce_flashing = true`, and the effective re-open interval at first launch is `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS_REDUCED` (CT-3). The Chart Table registers zero blocks, hooks, commands and mutators (CT-27).
391	*Source.* KRN CR-16; PCI:845; PIPE:301. **-> ADR candidate (c):** the store mechanism (a `ConfigFile` at `user://settings.cfg` is the working proposal; NOT SOURCEABLE in the engine reference) and its Alpha replacement.
392	
393	**CT-20. First-launch photosensitivity notice.**
394	*Rule.* Shown once, before the main menu, on the chart-table register, in the reading face (PIPE PR-13(e), PIPE:228). It offers the two toggles (reduce flashing, reduced motion) inline, with **reduce flashing shown already ON** (the first-launch default, CT-19; the player may turn it off here) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, and one dismiss action; no countdown, no auto-dismiss, no hold, no animated element (the notice is not itself a photosensitive stimulus), and **default focus on the dismiss action, not on a toggle** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the first input of the game is most likely a bare accept, and a state-flipping control under default focus would turn the shown-ON reduce-flashing protection OFF for exactly the player the D79 ruling protects. Both toggles stay reachable by navigation (NAV_UP from dismiss; the order is the two toggles, then dismiss), and a single `ACCEPT_DOWN` / `ACCEPT_UP` pair on first launch dismisses the notice, writes `notice_seen` and leaves `reduce_flashing = true` (AC-CT-131). **General rule:** no state-flipping control holds default focus on any screen reachable before the player's first deliberate input; this covers S9, the only such screen (S6, even when reached from the boot main menu, is entered through the player's own deliberate accept on the Display & Comfort item, and the CT-41(1) fresh-press latch keeps that press from activating its first control). The dismiss label must not be "Continue" (Save/Load's campaign verb, SL:993); it is a `ct.*` key. Dismissal writes `notice_seen` to the store. Copy is the UX spec's and the narrative director's; this GDD fixes only the behaviour. If the flag is absent the notice appears again; a second showing is identical (no state difference).
395	*Source.* PIPE PR-13(e); CON outside-playtester gate (CON:483).

397	#### E. Saving, campaigns and failures
398	
399	**CT-21. Save & Quit (UI-2 and UI-3 behaviour, verbatim).**
400	*Rule.* One action calls Save/Load's `save_and_quit()`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the call's blocking behaviour is stated.)* **Call contract (this layer's requirement of Save/Load, ASK-CT-7):** the layer disables every item and **presents one frame** before it makes the call, so the disabled styling is on screen before any work; the call must return promptly with `REFUSED_DOWNED` (the same fact as `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`) or `STARTED`, and report completion through a signal or the published `save_status` (`WRITTEN`, `FAILED`) rather than by blocking the frame loop for the write, because a blocked loop freezes the panel and invites an Alt-F4 mid-write. Save/Load's timeout `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` is Save/Load's value (5 000 ms at authoring, range 2 000-15 000 ms); this layer's requirement *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* is that the time to a visible `FAILED` be **3 000 ms or less**, because nothing visible is allowed during the wait (SL-24) and an up-to-5-s frozen-looking panel invites an Alt-F4 mid-write: the layer asks Save/Load for a **3 000 ms default** (ASK-CT-18; Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling G2, creative-director lean, horror-tone reasons), and AC-CT-137 fails a build whose default exceeds it. **Save/Load's `save_and_quit` itself calls `request_shutdown` after `WRITTEN`, or after an unchanged-state-hash skip that writes nothing (SL-6); the layer calls nothing on that path and never waits on `WRITTEN` as an exit guard.** The item is enabled iff `PauseGate.can_save_quit` (CT-4); otherwise it is disabled (the Hull Grey disabled style of CT-VA-7). While the write runs (state `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT`, this GDD's own label and not a Save/Load name) all items are disabled, `chart_table` and `cancel` are ignored, and **nothing is added to the screen**: no spinner, no ring, no bar, no percentage, no toast, no text change (SL UI-2; SL H5; SL-24). If any bound seat is `DOWNED` or `DEAD` (the `DEAD` case is unreachable in the solo MVP, SL-6), nothing is written and the result `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED` opens **`UI3_PLATE`**, the UI-3 message plate: a string stating that the newest autosave will be used (Continue restores the newest verified generation), **Back** (default focus, non-destructive) and **Quit without saving** (the destructive item, under hold-to-confirm, CT-22). A held or failed write (`SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS`, Save/Load's) lands in **`SAVE_FAILED`, which is the panel itself** with the plain word `FAILED` (a word, never colour, never Alarm Red: a save is not an instrument, HR-4) in the panel's status-line position (CT-17): the four items stay in CT-3 order, and Resume, Chart, Display & Comfort and `chart_table` all work (SL:785: "the pause panel stays"). Accepting Save & Quit there opens `UI3_PLATE` with **Retry** (default focus, non-destructive; to `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT`) and **Quit without saving** (hold). Completing the UI-3 hold calls `request_shutdown` once (CR-15) with no write; further input is ignored. `save_status` is a sticky read the layer never clears. `UI3_PLATE` is a full-bleed **message plate** (CT-28) in place of the panel *(orchestrator ruling: UI-3's string is a paragraph and the panel is too narrow for the 45-75 character reading measure at 4 of 6 canvases, ui-programmer finding X1 option (a); OQ-CT-12)*. No death language anywhere (SL:993 list).
401	*Source.* SL-6 (SL:195); SL UI-2, UI-3 (SL:998-999); SL H5, SL-24.
402	
403	**CT-22. Hold-to-confirm gesture (closes SL OQ-32 by citation).**
404	*Rule.* Destructive actions (UI-3 quit without saving; UI-5 retire and delete *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*) fill a **linear bar with a needle-mark**, never a radial wipe (ART 3.4, 7.3), over the action's hold duration *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` for UI-3 quit-without-saving and the UI-5 Retire *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and `DELETE_HOLD_S` (= 2 x `CONFIRM_HOLD_S`, 1.6 s at authoring) for UI-5 delete; both are Player Controller-owned constants and the second is a **proposed name** (value and range in the Tuning Knobs "cited, not ours" rows; Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D81, OQ-CT-30). Every hold-to-confirm also carries the **committed accessibility plan** (Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D80, OQ-CT-8): a two-tap alternative (PCI:835) and an adjustable hold duration, delivered at Alpha by the Controller and Accessibility Settings; the MVP layer ships the hold only, but D.2 reads its threshold from the action's effective duration (never a literal) so neither option needs a rebuild of the gesture. The action fires on the first frame the held time reaches it, not on release. Default focus on a screen with a destructive action is its non-destructive item. Release, `cancel`, `chart_table`, the pointer leaving the item, or window focus loss snaps the bar to empty in the same frame and **nothing else happens**; a new gesture needs a new press edge. The fill is a monotonic fill on the layer's UI clock (CT-43), not a flash (HR-13), and it is function rather than decoration so reduced motion does not remove it. Formula D.2.
405	*Clarification.* PCI:656 says "hold timers (confirm bar, name reveal) are frozen with the pause". That sentence concerns the Adapter's **in-world** channel timers; the UI-3 bar must run while the kernel is `PAUSED`, because the Chart Table is the only thing awake then. Routed to the Player Controller as a wording clarification (C15).
406	*Source.* SL UI-3, UI-5; ART 7.3, 7.4, HR-14; registry `CONFIRM_HOLD_S`; PCI:835.
407	
408	**CT-23. Main menu (UI-4).**
409	*Rule.* The boot menu has four items in fixed order: **Continue, New campaign, Display & Comfort, Quit** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: Display & Comfort is added so the comfort and photosensitivity toggles are reachable after the first launch without entering a live world, which is the reason the layer exists; it reuses S6, TX-36, TX-37, AC-CT-122)*. Continue is shown disabled (not hidden) when `campaign_info()` returns nothing; default focus is Continue if enabled, else New campaign. Continue shows exactly Save/Load UI-4's SIM facts as words, **without `RISKY`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: playtime (D.7, read on every `MAIN_MENU` entry (re-read after a FAULTED return, a failed `new_game` or a Display & Comfort return, TX-34, TX-37; never refreshed while the menu stays open) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), crew count, kind (`AUTO` / `EVENT` / `QUIT`) and `depth_label` (`RING <n>`).
410	*`RISKY` is not on the Continue line — ruled* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): `RISKY` is dropped from the player-facing Continue line (OQ-CT-31, D82; the creative-director's lean is adopted). It is a fact about the **file** (the generation was written while a soft gate condition was closed, SL-6), not about the world, and it could read as a world-danger or tell-state leak onto the truth layer (a breach was open when the record was written) with no decision attached to it (a single Continue). It stays in `SaveInfo` and in the Debug Overlay; this layer neither reads nor draws it, and the Continue line is exactly playtime, crew count, kind and `RING <n>`. Save/Load's UI-4 is amended to match (hand-off note). **`RING <n>` is the ring of the newest record's pod / home position at the time that record was written; it is never a maximum, a historical "deepest reached" or any running aggregate over the campaign** (G5; a later record at a shallower ring shows the shallower ring; AC-CT-113). No thumbnail, no completion figure, no wall-clock "last played" beyond file metadata. The UI-7 line is shown under Continue on menu entry iff `campaign_info()` reports the newest generation failed verification (`newest_failed_verification`, accepted by Save/Load SL-21; ASK-CT-5 answered). One Continue serves the one logical autosave: the generation chain is invisible and never chosen (UI-4's own wording uses another noun; the stale-token lint allow-list carries it). Vocabulary is Save/Load's only (SL:993). `new_game(world_seed)` takes its seed from Save/Load's boot rule; the menu has no seed field (OQ-CT-6). The backdrop reuses the depth-ring plate and the ring-1 filament sheet with **no nodes** (a node would imply a save state or leak a Continue fact); fallback plain Ground. No title art, logo animation or tagline.
411	*Source.* SL UI-4 (SL:1000), SL-21 (SL:261); ART 2.11.
412	
413	**CT-24. New campaign, UI-5, no beam picker.**
414	*Rule.* New campaign with no existing campaign calls `new_game(world_seed)` directly (via CT-42). With an existing campaign it opens the **UI-5 screen** itself: items **Back** (**default focus**), **Retire** (**under hold-to-confirm at `CONFIRM_HOLD_S`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: at MVP the player experiences it as irreversible, because Continue stops listing the campaign and there is **no un-retire screen**; the file stays on disk but nothing in the game brings it back, and no text calls it "reversible" or "archived"), and **Delete** as a separate explicit action on the same screen under the longer hold (CT-22). The UI-5 sentence (a `ct.*` key, copy the UX spec's and narrative director's) states plainly what each item does to the player's ability to continue: Back keeps the campaign and Continue still lists it; Retire (hold) takes it off Continue and the game cannot bring it back; Delete (longer hold) destroys the file *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the word "Retire" suggests a recoverable archive, so the vocabulary is routed to Save/Load (OQ-CT-39) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the default moves from Retire to Back, because the old default let a double-tap on New campaign retire the campaign; the fresh-press-edge rule of CT-41(1) now applies to **every** boot transition, so the press that opened UI-5 never activates an item on it)*. Retire and delete call `retire_campaign(campaign_id)` / `delete_campaign(campaign_id)`; the retired state `RETIRED` is caused by this layer (SL T-9, SL:430). The retired file survives and Continue stops listing it (AC-CT-128). The Delete hold is **longer than the quit hold** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): Delete (UI-5) holds `DELETE_HOLD_S` = 2 x `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` = 1.6 s at authoring (OQ-CT-30, D81), while quit-without-saving (UI-3) keeps `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` (0.8 s). Delete is the one action that destroys the file with no recovery even by hand, so it asks for twice the hold of the quit that leaves the file on disk; D.2 works the arithmetic. The destructive items (Retire and Delete) look like every other list item (no red, no warning mark) and are distinguished by the bar only *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. No campaign list, Records page or un-retire screen at MVP (OQ-CT-4: a retired file stays on disk and is recoverable by file only until an Alpha screen; no text calls retire "reversible"). No beam-shape picker: New campaign calls nothing beyond `new_game`; seat defaults are Suit & Equipment's (SE-9: seat 1 `BEAM_WIDE`); a `NewCampaignOptions` seam is reserved for the VS-B picker (SE:189 calls it optional).
415	*Source.* SL UI-5 (SL:1001); SE-9 (SE:189).
416	
417	**CT-25. Load-failure screens (boot-flow).**
418	*Rule.* UI-8 (`SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE`: a plain statement that no readable record exists, with New campaign and Quit, in that order) and UI-9 (incompatible build: message, New campaign and Quit, in that order, never overwrite or repair; the item order is the same on both screens, which removes the earlier flip between UI-8 and UI-9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* are **boot-flow screens**: no pause is requested because the kernel is not `RUNNING` when the failure is reported (SL:1004 says "Chart Table issues the pause"; that wording is stale, C7). UI-7 (corrupt newest record) is one plain ship-log line under the Continue entry **iff** `campaign_info()` reports that the newest generation failed verification (`campaign_info().newest_failed_verification`, SL-21; ASK-CT-5 answered); otherwise the line is HUD & Suit Layer's on the first `RUNNING` frame (SL:1003 lists both owners; this GDD owns the main-menu instance only). New campaign from UI-9 calls `new_game(world_seed)` through CT-42 without opening UI-5; Save/Load creates a different directory and the `READ_ONLY` campaign is never retired, deleted or written (SL:752, SL T-9). Placeholder strings are Save/Load's (SL:1003-1005); final copy is this GDD's `ct.*` table with UX and narrative sign-off. No icon, no red, no dialog chrome beyond the standard Ground plate.
419	*Source.* SL UI-7..UI-9; SL:770.
420	
421	**CT-26. FAULTED in release.**
422	*Rule.* The destination is the boot-flow **main menu** (UI-4) with Continue offered, focus on Continue: in `FAULTED` the kernel never writes or autosaves over an existing save (KRN:151), so the newest verified generation is intact. Whether a one-line notice accompanies it is OQ-CT-5 (routed to the kernel and Save/Load); this GDD invents no string. Dev builds halt with the Debug Overlay (not ours). PIPE:269 says release "returns to the chart table" and KRN:151 says "returns to the menu"; the wording is reconciled by this rule and routed (C14).
423	*Source.* KRN:151, :940; PIPE:269.
424	
425	**CT-42. The load sequence: black before work.**
426	*Rule.* Accepting Continue, New campaign, Retire (then New) or Delete (then New): (1) all items are disabled and the layer's plate is removed in the same frame; (2) layer 1 black is shown (PIPE row 1: shown in `TRANSIT_HOLD` and `BOOTING/LOADING`); (3) at least one frame at full black is presented (the mechanism is the Pipeline's `TRANSIT_HOLD` guarantee, `t_hold_pad` of at least 120 ms, which the layer awaits before step (4); the layer does not count frames itself, and the test hook is the frame-capture hook of AC-CT-60; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*); (4) only then is `continue_campaign()` / `new_game(world_seed)` called; (5) the first `RUNNING` frame is a camera `CUT` (PIPE:264) and the layer leaves `LOAD_HOLD` for `CLOSED` (TX-33). Nothing is drawn between (2) and (5): no text, no tip, no bar, no spinner (SL UI-6). If the call returns UI-8 or UI-9 the layer re-enables itself on that boot screen (TX-11); if `new_game` (or any other call) fails it re-enables itself on the main menu with one plain ship-log line under New campaign (placeholder copy "Could not start a new campaign.", final copy the UX spec's and the narrative director's; TX-34, OQ-CT-17 closed). A load that fell back from a corrupt newest generation is not a failure: it proceeds to `RUNNING` and the UI-7 line is the HUD's on the first `RUNNING` frame (CT-25) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
427	*Why.* A restore called with a visible, focused menu would freeze that menu for the whole restore, and a long non-pumping call can mark the window "not responding" on Windows (NOT SOURCEABLE). Save/Load has answered ASK-CT-7: the kernel's restore and every `post_restore()` run as one blocking call inside `LOADING`, never chunked, and the one presented black frame is the Pipeline's `TRANSIT_HOLD` guarantee (`t_hold_pad`); the rule needs only that one black frame, never progress *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
428	*Source.* SL UI-6; PIPE:99, :264, :278.
429	
430	#### F. Registrations, strings and access
431	
432	**CT-27. Zero registrations; submits nothing.**
433	*Rule.* The chart table is an `INPUT_SURFACE` (KRN:111; PIPE:188; PCI:147) that **submits zero commands at MVP**; the class is kept for VS-B guest pause / save requests (KRN CR-15). It registers **no state block, no hook, no command, no mutator**, and introduces no `allowed_when_paused` type (so KRN CR-16's paused-allowed list is unchanged). It reads only `web.view`, `SaveInfo`, `save_status`, `restore_reason`, `campaign_info()` / `list_saves()` and its own host-local state; never `web.leg_timing()`. It calls only the kernel control plane (`request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_shutdown`) and Save/Load's host-local API (`new_game`, `continue_campaign`, `save_and_quit`, `retire_campaign`, `delete_campaign`). KRN:715 offers "a chart-table command with a path array" as a `MAX_PAYLOAD` example: that example is stale (C3) because this layer submits no command.
434	*Source.* KRN CR-15; SL-21; WM:300; SL-17 (the zero-block precedent).
435	
436	**CT-28. Strings, faces and fit.**
437	*Rule.* All user-visible strings are keys in a closed `ct.*` table owned here (`tr()`), ship-log register, no composed fragments (a value token such as a time is allowed inside one whole string), no exclamation marks, no emoji, Save/Load's vocabulary only. **Instrument face** (bitmap, integer `H`): a closed string set, declared in the `ct.*` table, of `IN TRANSIT`, numerals, keycap letters and short state words; **reading face** (vector, continuous scale): panel item labels, settings copy, the notice, messages and every sentence (ART 7.1). Type and contrast floors are ART 7.1's, by name (menu body, section heading, title, label and caption floors at 1080p / 1440p; text 4.5:1, glyphs 3:1). Each key carries a **fit class**: `LABEL_1` (one line at every canvas row), `LABEL_2` (up to two lines) or `PARAGRAPH` (message plates only, full-bleed Ground sized to the text with the ART 7.1 line-length measure). A lint measures each key with the real faces at each canvas row of CT-16 and fails a `LABEL_1` that overflows; a menu label is never truncated or ellipsised (a clipped "Save & Qu" on the truth layer would read as a lie) and never wraps to a third line.
438	*Source.* SL:127, :993, :1008; ART 7.1.
439	
440	**CT-29. Audio: requests only.**
441	*Rule.* This layer owns and specifies no sound. It requests from Adaptive Audio a UI-bus focus-move cue, a confirm cue and the queued-re-open acknowledgement `UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED` (CT-3) (AA:562: "menu and map sounds are UI-bus, ducked out of the world mix on open; pause suspends all sim-derived sounds"); nothing for open, save or load. `UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED` is one-shot, on the `ui` bus, with no visual twin, no sanity-stage or Attention dependence, and identical at `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` 334 and `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS_REDUCED` 1000; the Chart Table requests it on the press frame that puts a raise into the empty re-open queue, or replaces the queued raise with a different desired raise, once per queued raise; it is SILENT for an idempotent repeat of the same desired raise, for `cancel` of the queue, for the frame on which the queue applies the raise (the plate is the feedback), for a raise that applies at once (no lower within the interval) and for a `request_restore` that clears the queue (TX-27) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G2/G6: CT-3 queued acknowledgement, ASK-CT-20)*. Ducking on open and suspension of sim sounds on pause are Adaptive Audio's. Silent menus are acceptable at MVP. No sanity or Attention effect on menu audio. The master volume control (CT-18, Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D85) only publishes a step through the `SettingsStore`: the bus, the step-to-gain law, the default, the muted state and any cue played at the new level are Adaptive Audio's, and the layer plays nothing itself *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
442	*Source.* AA:562, AA:1086; HR-6. *(provisional — Adaptive Audio owns the cues.)*
443	
444	**CT-30. Accessibility at MVP (structural).**
445	*Rule.* Now: opaque Ground plates (HR-2), focus as a shape (HR-11), ART 7.1 type and contrast floors (HR-12), gamepad completeness of every flow including the chart snap and every destructive action (HR-14), no colour-only state (SL:1010), and an **accessible name on every interactive control** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier "a text label on every control" was false for chart nodes, which by CT-14 carry no label)*. **Every focusable chart node is a `Control` with an accessible name equal to its neutral ordinal** (the `ct.compact.slot_<n>` key form of CT-44, **nothing drawn**, so G6 and CT-14 hold in the spatial layout); a node is never built as a bare quad, so adding the AccessKit wiring later forces no rebuild. Every other control's accessible name is its visible `ct.*` label. Mouse and touch players get a signal for what is selectable through the **pointer cursor** change over selectable nodes only (CT-45; OQ-CT-9 closed). At Alpha (Accessibility Settings / Settings): AccessKit wiring (NOT SOURCEABLE in the engine reference; an ADR (e) spike item), hold-duration and two-tap alternatives for every hold-to-confirm (the destructive holds of UI-3 and UI-5; the Controller's two-tap option, PCI), HUD opacity floor, reading-face scale, HUD scale. **Accessibility tier: standard** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): OQ-CT-8, D80). `design/accessibility-requirements.md` does not exist yet and is to be authored later with `/ux-design accessibility` (it is not created here); until then the layer targets the structural compliance listed above plus the committed Alpha items: a two-tap alternative and an adjustable hold duration for every hold-to-confirm (CT-22), and reduce flashing ON by default (CT-19, a user ruling).

446	*Source.* ART HR-2, HR-11, HR-12, HR-14; SL:1010.
447	
448	#### G. Negative requirements (each its own rule, each with an acceptance criterion in Acceptance Criteria)
449	
450	**CT-31. No Attention surface.** *Rule.* No Attention indicator, meter, tier, hint or glyph on any chart, panel or menu surface, under any setting; depth rings are shown as place, not as attention; no Chart Table surface displays or sonifies the Attention level, tell progress or a Horror's proximity (AA:1515); no per-write autosave mark (its absence would be a hidden Attention meter, SL:965). *Source.* AT:1373, AC-AT-61, AC-AT-66; AA:1515 (Adaptive Audio UI Requirements, "depth rings are place, not attention"); ART 7.4.
451	**CT-32. No horror element (Pillar 3).** *Rule.* No horror, horror position, threat bar, proximity indicator, direction, off-screen arrow, countdown, "last seen" pin or target ring on any chart or menu surface, **under any accessibility setting**. *Source.* HE:377, :1353, :1358, AC-HE-119; Pillar 3 (Attention is shown in the world, never as a meter).
452	**CT-33. No loot value, no remaining-salvage count.** *Rule.* The Chart Table picks the target and shows only what the crew lit, and never reveals; this confirms Boarding's provisional contract (BS:334, Dependencies row 17b); no loot value, no remaining-salvage count (BS:334; BS:1204's wording "and the fuel the hop will cost" is overruled by CT-35, C1). *Source.* BS:334, AC-BS-47c (BS:1427), WM-28, ART 7.4.
453	**CT-34. No sanity indicator.** *Rule.* No sanity meter, bar, ring, number, icon or colour on any surface of this layer, including under accessibility settings; save and pause surfaces are never a hallucination class. *Source.* SN:1350, :1357, AC-SN-83, SL H6.
454	**CT-35. No fuel, time, ETA, danger or "recommended".** *Rule.* No fuel figure, travel time, ETA, danger rating or "recommended" marker anywhere on the chart; `web.view` structurally lacks the data and the chart never reads `web.leg_timing()`. Boarding's row BS:1204 ("the Chart Table shows what the crew lit and the fuel the hop will cost") conflicts and **Web Map & Transit governs** (WM:1049, WM-35, AB-5; routed to Boarding to reword). *Source.* WM:1049, :1299, :1305; WM-36; C1.
455	**CT-36. No save decoration.** *Rule.* No per-write autosave mark, thumbnail, spinner, percentage, death screen, "progress saved" toast or loading text or tip. Load is layer-1 black via `TRANSIT_HOLD` (UI-6), then a camera `CUT`; this layer adds nothing after a death-stub restore; the **HUD** owns one plain ship-log line on the first `RUNNING` frame, keyed on `restore_reason = DEATH_STUB`, through its `FIRST_FRAME_LINE` channel, with no death wording (placeholder copy "Restored from the newest record.") *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): SL OQ-46 option (b), OQ-CT-33, D84; a death-restart with no text can read as a crash or a rubber-band, which sits badly with the tone row "plain honesty about the cost". The line is the HUD's, so the layer still shows no death screen, counter or word *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Source.* SL H5, SL:965, SL-24 (SL:267); SL UI-6; ART 2.10.
456	**CT-37. No inventory, weight or loadout screen.** *Rule.* No inventory, weight readout or loadout screen. The Sanity evidence list (SN:1350, SN:1357) names "the inventory" and "the death/restore screen"; neither exists (IDB R8; SE:1289; SL; ART), routed to Sanity (C8). *Source.* IDB R8 (IDB:1065, :1320); SE:1289, :1317.
457	
458	#### H. Reserved slots and the rules added by the specialists
459	
460	**CT-38. Reserved slots (no stub art, no layout space at MVP).**
461	
462	| Slot | Owner and phase | Constraint carried |
463	|---|---|---|
464	| Crew beam-shape glyphs on the chart; left-edge text chat | Co-op Session / Chat (VS-B) | ART 7.4, 7.5; risk K1 |
465	| Knowledge Codex annotations | Codex (VS) | each annotation needs a stated effect on play (IDX:47) and is never a lore dump on the truth layer; PROFILE scope |
466	| Post-loss UI read at the chart table | Failure Contract & Re-wake (VS-A) | ART 7.4 "Loss" |
467	| Onboarding flow after the notice | Onboarding (VS) | `POD_NOT_READY` reserved in Web Map & Transit |
468	| Beam-shape picker | VS-B | `NewCampaignOptions` seam |
469	| Records page, un-retire | Alpha | OQ-CT-4 |
470	| Full PR-14 settings UI, rebinding, HUD scale | Settings & Input Rebinding (Alpha) | MVP hooks with defaults |
471	
472	**CT-39. Narrow truth.** *Rule.* The layer displays only facts that no hallucination class can lie about. Every field it draws is listed with its source (`web.view`, `SaveInfo`, `save_status`, `restore_reason`, `campaign_info()`, the `SettingsStore`) and with the statement that no hallucination class touches it; a fact that any class can falsify (Graph state, entity presence or position, salvage contents or value, a crewmate's rendered form or location) never enters the layer. *Why.* A true copy of a falsifiable fact on a free, pausable menu would make that lie free to disprove, and P4 requires that checking cost time, risk or trust. Review test: *if a hallucination could make the world disagree with this field, the field does not belong here.* *Source.* CON:261-265; Player Fantasy "Under hallucination".
473	
474	**CT-40. Constant drift, constant depth.** *Rule.* The filament drift step and the ring tones are independent of every simulation read and of Attention, depth, sanity and session time; the only inputs to the drift are the layer's UI clock and the reduced-motion toggle. *Why.* P3 names "filament movement" as an in-world Attention sign; a chart filament that modulated would be a meter. *Source.* AT:1373; ART 2.11.
475	
476	**CT-41. Input hygiene around the irreversible press.**
477	*Rule* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: guards (1) to (3) and (5) are enforced by the Adapter's MenuInput feed, CT-45; the layer states the behaviour it needs and consumes the events)*. (1) **Fresh press edge.** When the layer is opened by a console press or by a released governor raise, every activation on it requires a press edge that begins after the open frame; the open press's release, its auto-repeat and any carried-over held state are ignored (the Adapter latches them, CT-45). (2) **The closing activation is consumed.** When `interact` on Resume, `chart_table` or `cancel` at depth 1 closes the layer, the Adapter emits nothing from that control, to the layer or to gameplay, until it is physically released and pressed again; gameplay sees no `interact` edge until a fresh press. The layer **cannot** enforce this alone, because the Adapter polls and resyncs on resume. (3) **Echo ignored.** The Esc / Start toggle's key echo is suppressed by the Adapter, so a held Esc does not flicker the layer. PCI resends intents on resume and keeps a hold-mode channel only if the button is physically down, so the latch belongs to the Adapter and the layer's requirement is stated here. Every delta is clamped to `UI_DT_MAX_MS` `[PLACEHOLDER]` so a hitch cannot complete a hold or jump the drift. 485	**CT-44. The compact layout and stable order.**
486	*Status: **DEFERRED-REACHABLE*** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: at `H_default` every supported window (minimum 1280 x 720, registry `MIN_WINDOW`) gives `m >= 1` (D.1b "Minimum window"), so a player cannot reach the compact list at MVP; it is built and tested through the forced-`H` hook and becomes player-reachable with the Alpha HUD scale or a window delivered below the minimum. This rule, S4, the neutral ordinals, ASK-CT-10 and AC-CT-30 / AC-CT-112 are tagged accordingly.
487	*Rule.* The layout is **compact iff the chart multiplier `m` (D.1b, the fit inequalities) is below 1**, i.e. the frame plus its margins no longer fits the canvas; nominally that is a canvas narrower than 320 HUD px (`COMPACT_LAYOUT_MIN_CANVAS_W`, `[PLACEHOLDER]`, **derived** as `CHART_FRAME` width / 0.9, with the height twin 180 = 162 / 0.9; informational since the fit form replaced it as the input to `m`) or shorter than its twin; it is chosen at open and on canvas change, never mid-animation. The list holds at most `N_max_compact` rows (3 at the smallest canvases, D.1b). Then the spatial map is replaced by a **vertical node list** in the ART 7.4 menu grammar: one column of chamfered-rectangle items, Ground interiors, 1-px Graphite-lit borders, the bracket and bezel thickening for focus, each item carrying its 24x24 node glyph at left (the unknown tick drawn inside the silhouette exactly as on the map) and a **neutral positional ordinal** at right (a slot mark, below). The ring plate's Ground, border and rivets remain; rings and filaments are not drawn. The planned-sortie relation is a Tungsten dashed rule under the picked row (no new asset, no fill). The `IN TRANSIT` word keeps its fixed top-left position. **The compact label is a neutral positional ordinal and carries no identity.** It is one whole `ct.*` key per authored layout slot (`ct.compact.slot_<n>`, `n` = the record's position in the layout file, HOME included; no composed fragment such as a word plus a number, CT-28), rendered as the plain ordinal for that slot. It must not be a name, a dialect, a template word or a status word, and it never varies with `status`, `kind`, `template_id`, depth ring or map distance: **an UNSEEN row and a SEEN row render the identical key form**, and a record's key does not change when it becomes SEEN, BOARDED, `berthed` or ORPHAN. The key is bound to the layout slot and is not renumbered when an ABSORBED record leaves the list (a gap in the ordinals is a fact the list already shows, and a stable slot mark lets the player remember which row is which). The ordinal order is lint-checked like positions (no correlation with any Web Map & Transit cost; AC-CT-112). This is the single permitted exception to G6 and CT-14 ("except the CT-44 neutral ordinal in the compact layout, which is not a name"); it is **not** precedent for any further label. WM:1044 (UNSEEN "no dialect, no tick, no label beyond what selection shows") is read as forbidding identity, which a slot mark does not carry (text-label rule of CT-30; **accepted by Web Map & Transit**: its UNSEEN drawing row names the neutral ordinal as the single exception, ASK-CT-10 answered). **Order is a ranking proxy and is therefore fixed:** the list is in stable authored order, HOME first, derelicts in layout-file order; it is never sorted by status, distance, fuel, danger, recency or seen/unseen; an ABSORBED record leaves the list (it is part of HOME now), an ORPHAN stays in its slot, non-selectable; the relative order of the remaining rows never changes. Rows are never truncated; if the list cannot fit, the canvas minimum was mis-set.

492	**CT-45. Menu input feed (Adapter-owned)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; new rule)*.
493	*Rule.* **The layer never reads a device.** The Input Adapter (Player Controller & Input PC-1(a)) owns every device read and publishes a presentation-side **MenuInput** event stream on **render frames** (the layer runs on its own UI clock while the kernel is `PAUSED`, CT-43; the Adapter's physics-callback sampling serves gameplay intents only). The stream is the layer's only input, because the Controller's locked lint allows `Input.`, `InputMap.`, `InputEvent` handling, `_input(`, `_unhandled_input(` and `is_action_*` only inside the Adapter's registered files (PCI Acceptance, source-scan criterion). Events: `NAV_DOWN{dir, source}` and `NAV_UP{dir}` (`dir` UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT; `source` STICK, DPAD, ARROW, WASD); `ACCEPT_DOWN` and `ACCEPT_UP`; `BACK`; `CLOSE`; `FOCUS_OUT` and `FOCUS_IN`; `DEVICE_CHANGED{device}`; `POINTER{kind MOVE|DOWN|UP|WHEEL, button, position in picture coordinates}`.
494	- **The Adapter also owns**: (1) **echo suppression** (a held key's OS echo produces no second event; CT-41(3)); (2) **deadzone hysteresis** (`MOVE_DEADZONE` to take an edge, `MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT` to release it); (3) **the cardinal-axis rule** (a stick yields one NAV direction at a time: the axis with the larger magnitude, a tie going to the vertical axis, and the taken direction changes only after the stick has re-passed `MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`, so a diagonal drift cannot alternate between two directions); (4) **latch-until-released** for any physical control whose press closed the layer (Resume's accept, `chart_table`, `cancel`): the Adapter emits nothing from that control, to the layer or to gameplay, until it has been physically released and pressed again. 495	- **Navigation set, per device.** Stick (cardinal, edge at `MOVE_DEADZONE`), D-pad (four buttons), arrow keys, and WASD (the `move_*` physical controls). **Accept** = the physical controls of `interact` in this context: E, gamepad A, and Enter and Space as additional keyboard bindings of the context's accept. **Mouse buttons produce `POINTER` events only, never `ACCEPT`** (this GDD's requirement): LMB is not an accept in the `chart_table` context. The Controller's `chart_table` context note currently lists LMB as an alias of `interact` (E / LMB / A), so a change is requested of the Controller (ASK-CT-15) and recorded as conflict row C23; so a pointer click and a pad accept are two paths that cannot both fire for one physical press (EC-CT-15). **Back** = `cancel` (X / B). **Close** = `chart_table` (Esc / Start). The **D-pad is navigation** in this context: the d-pad zoom edges of PC-16 are emitted from `gameplay` and `inspect_card` only (the PC-2 context table: zoom ignored here), so no zoom edge reaches the layer and none must be discarded by it (EC-CT-18). A pad or Deck player moves the bracket on a vertical list by stick, D-pad or the keyboard equivalents, with no diagonal ambiguity.
496	- **Pointer.** The layer hit-tests `POINTER` events against its own rectangles; a click is an activation only when the UP lands on the item that received the DOWN (EC-CT-16; the full activation rules are in "Activation, reveal and focus targets" below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; hover turns a label Tungsten and hides the bracket (CT-6). A selectable chart node shows the **pointer cursor** (a cursor-shape change only, no art, no label), which closes OQ-CT-9.
497	- **One focus model** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The layer's focus is the only focus, and the mechanism is decided here (option 1 of the re-review): **every layer-3 `Control` is created with `focus_mode = FOCUS_NONE` and `mouse_filter = MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE`**, so the engine's focus owner is never a layer-3 `Control`, the built-in `ui_*` actions have no focus to move, and the engine's own hover and click routing never reaches the layer (all pointer input arrives as `POINTER` events, hit-tested by the layer). The layer draws and tracks its single focus itself as a retained control id (the bracket is drawn from that id). The **accessible-focus path** (CT-30) is separate from engine focus: the layer publishes the retained control id and its `ct.*` accessible name to the accessibility layer through the per-item accessible-name properties, with no engine focus involved; whether AccessKit exposes and announces a `FOCUS_NONE` control's name is **[UNV]** and is spike item (2). Layer-3 Controls take no raw `gui_input`, and the layer neither consumes nor relies on any `ui_*` action. The earlier "engine focus may be mirrored" allowance is **deleted**: a `Control` that holds engine focus is exactly what Godot moves on `ui_down`, so mirroring cannot coexist with AC-CT-118. The rejected alternative (option 2, the Adapter consuming `ui_*` in `_input`) would keep engine focus live and add a second consumer to the Adapter's registered files. Engine specifics (the 4.6 split of mouse/touch and keyboard/gamepad focus, `modules/ui.md`; `FOCUS_NONE` Controls and the accessible-name path) are **[UNV]** until the ADR (e) spike on 4.7.2.

A mouse-only or Deck-touch player therefore completes every hold flow by pressing and holding the item; a click released before the threshold does nothing. (d) **Disabled items are focusable but inert** (accept does nothing; the Hull Grey disabled style of CT-VA-7); in `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT` nothing is focusable and the bracket is hidden (CT-21). (e) **Focus targets after a transition:** TX-23 (to `SAVE_FAILED`): Resume; TX-25: Retry; TX-32 and TX-39 (to `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT`): none; TX-19 (back to `PANEL`): the item that led to the screen just left (Chart, Display & Comfort or Save & Quit); TX-37: the Display & Comfort item. (g) **Read phase.** The Adapter delivers one render frame's MenuInput events in arrival order at the start of that frame, before the layer's per-frame update, so a press and the state it acts on are the same frame's.
499	- **Repeat.** Auto-repeat of a held NAV direction is the layer's, from `NAV_DOWN` and `NAV_UP`, on its UI clock (D.9).

501	*Source.* PC-1(a), PC-2, PC-13, PC-16, PCI source-scan criterion; `modules/ui.md`, `modules/input.md`. **ASK-CT-15 to the Player Controller & Input** (new): publish the MenuInput stream, the echo, hysteresis, cardinal-axis and latch rules above, and the Enter and Space accept bindings.

576	**Reachability and closure checks (for the acceptance criteria).** Every state has an exit that does not depend on a hold: `HOLD_CONFIRM` exits by release; `UI3_PLATE` exits by `cancel`, `chart_table`, Retry or Back; `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT` exits when Save/Load's `save_and_quit` ends the process (SL-6) or by `FAILED` / the timeout of TX-23 (a Save/Load guarantee); the boot-flow screens each offer Quit. There is no state with no player input and no external exit except `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT` and `LOAD_HOLD`, both bounded by Save/Load results; `LOAD_HOLD` now has its exits in the table (TX-33 on the first `RUNNING` frame, TX-11 and TX-34 on a failure result) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A restore from any state lands in CLOSED (TX-27), and the first `RUNNING` frame after `LOADING` is a camera `CUT` (PIPE:264). **The transition table is data.** It lives in `assets/data/ui/chart_table_transitions.json` (path provisional; one record per TX id with `from`, `to`, `trigger`, `guard_id`, `effects[]`), is the single source the layer's state machine is built from, and is the file AC-CT-93 walks; the expected-edge fixture `tests/fixtures/chart_table/expected_edges.json` (provisional) lists every `(from, trigger, to)` triple of this section, so a missing or extra row fails the build by diff, not by a walker's silence *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
577	
578	**Order of presentation on boot.** TX-2 (notice) precedes TX-3 (menu); the menu precedes any session; the notice is never shown mid-session. FAULTED in release (TX-3) skips the notice when it has been seen.

700	The hold-to-confirm fill formula is defined as:
701	
702	`t_us(n+1) = t_us(n) + min(dt_us, UI_DT_MAX_MS * 1000) while the activation is physically down and the pointer or focus stays on the item; fill = clamp(t_us / (HOLD_S * 1000000), 0, 1); needle_px = min(floor(fill * L_BAR_HUD), L_BAR_HUD - 1); the action fires on the first frame with t_us >= HOLD_S * 1000000; HOLD_S = CONFIRM_HOLD_S for UI-3 and for the UI-5 Retire *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and DELETE_HOLD_S = min(2 * CONFIRM_HOLD_S, HOLD_EFF_MAX_S) for the UI-5 Delete *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*; release, cancel, chart_table, pointer exit or focus loss sets t_us = 0 in the same frame`
703	
704	**Variables:**
705	
706	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
707	|---|---|---|---|---|
708	| `t_us` | int, microseconds of UI process time | 0 to the threshold | this layer (CT-43); **not** simulation time, runs while the kernel is `PAUSED` | the held time on the layer's own clock |
709	| `dt_us` | int, microseconds | 0 to unbounded | the render delta | the frame delta before clamping |
710	| `UI_DT_MAX_MS` | int, ms | 33-100, default 50 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | the per-frame delta clamp (CT-43) |
711	| `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` | float, seconds | per the registry (Tuning Knobs, cited rows): 0.6-1.9 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* | Player Controller, registry constant (cited, not retuned) | the quit-without-saving hold duration (UI-3); the same constant that closes SL OQ-32 |
712	| `DELETE_HOLD_S` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)* | float, seconds | `min(2 * CONFIRM_HOLD_S, HOLD_EFF_MAX_S)` (the Controller's effective-hold rule `H_v = min(m_v * base, HOLD_EFF_MAX_S)`, `m_v` 2, `HOLD_EFF_MAX_S` 1.9 s): **1.2-1.9** over the Controller's base range 0.6-1.9 (the cap binds from a base of 0.95 s), 1.6 at authoring | Player Controller (proposed name, derived, not yet registered; Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D81) | the Delete hold duration (UI-5). Derived so that Delete is longer than quit-without-saving at every base below the 1.9 s ceiling (equal to it only at a base of 1.9 s, where the cap binds both) and so that an accessibility hold-duration option scales both together |
713	| `HOLD_S` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | float, seconds | per action | calculated | the threshold of the action being held; the one place the gesture reads its duration |
714	| `L_BAR_HUD` | int, HUD px | 32-96, default 64 `[PLACEHOLDER]`; capped at `P_w div H - 2 * safe_x` | this GDD | the bar length; the bar sits on a full-bleed message plate (`UI3_PLATE`, UI-5), not inside the 71-px panel |
