718	
719	**Example** (using the registry value of `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` at authoring, 0.8 s, so the threshold is 800,000 microseconds; the number is illustrative and the constant is the Controller's). At 60 fps, `dt_us = 16,667`. Frame 24: `t_us = 400,008`, `fill = 0.500`, `needle_px = floor(0.5 * 64) = 32`. Frame 47: `t_us = 783,349`, not yet. Frame 48: `t_us = 800,016 >= 800,000`, **fires**. Release at frame 30: `t_us = 0`, no action. Hitch: one 400 ms frame is clamped to 50 ms, so `fill` rises by 0.0625 and a stall can never complete a hold. At 10 fps (`dt_us = 100,000` clamped to 50,000) the bar advances at half real time and the hold takes 1.6 s: accepted, because a layer below 20 fps is already a failed frame budget. At either end of the Controller's range the same arithmetic holds with the threshold replaced. **Example, Delete (UI-5)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: `HOLD_S` = 1.6 s, so the threshold is 1,600,000 microseconds. At 60 fps (`dt_us` 16,667): frame 48 `t_us` = 800,016, `fill` = 0.500, `needle_px` = 32; frame 95 `t_us` = 1,583,365, not yet; frame 96 `t_us` = 1,600,032, **fires**. At 30 fps (`dt_us` 33,333): frame 48 = 1,599,984, not yet; frame 49 fires. At 10 fps (`dt_us` clamped to 50,000): frame 32, i.e. **3.2 s of wall time** (the 1.6 s above is the quit hold's 16 frames at 100 ms each; the two 1.6 figures are different quantities). Over the Controller's range, `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` 0.6 s gives a Delete hold of 1.2 s (frame 72 at 60 fps); a base of 0.95 s or more gives the capped 1.9 s (frame 114), so 1.2 s no longer gives 2.4 s (`H_v = min(m_v * base, HOLD_EFF_MAX_S)`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*. Constraint satisfied: `DELETE_HOLD_S > CONFIRM_HOLD_S` at every base below 1.9 s; at a base of 1.9 s both holds are 1.9 s (the cap) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*. **Delete-over-quit margin** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the cap collapses the margin exactly for the players who raised their hold duration for accessibility (the Alpha option), so this layer requires `DELETE_HOLD_S - CONFIRM_HOLD_S >= DELETE_MARGIN_MIN_S` (0.4 s `[PLACEHOLDER]`, constraint C-10) and asks the Controller to keep the **quit** hold's own cap at or below `HOLD_EFF_MAX_S - DELETE_MARGIN_MIN_S` = 1.5 s (ASK-CT-19); the authoring values (0.8 s and 1.6 s) already satisfy it (margin 0.8 s), and no ruled value changes.

721	### D.3 Snap-to-node
722	
723	The snap-to-node formula is defined as:
724	
725	`d = (x_c - x_f, y_f - y_c); phi = atan2(d.y, d.x) in degrees; delta = ((phi - theta + 540) mod 360) - 180 in [-180, 180); S1 = { c in F : -SNAP_SECTOR_DEG/2 <= delta(c) < +SNAP_SECTOR_DEG/2 }; S2 = { c in F : |delta(c)| < 90 }; chosen = argmin over (dist(f, c), |delta(c)|, ordinal(c)) lexicographically, over S1 if S1 is non-empty, else over S2 if S2 is non-empty, else the focus stays`
726	
727	**Variables:**
728	
729	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
730	|---|---|---|---|---|
731	| `f` | node | the focused node | this layer | where focus is now |
732	| `F` | set of nodes | the focusable nodes except `f` | D.4 plus HOME (CT-11 table) | the candidates; ORPHAN, berthed and absorbed records are not in it |
733	| `(x, y)` | int, frame art px, screen y down | frame-local | `chart_layout.json` (CT-12) | authored positions; `d.y` flips so that up is positive |
734	| `theta` | deg | 0 (right), 90 (up), 180 (left), 270 (down) | the pressed direction | cardinal navigation (CT-5); a `NAV_DOWN{dir}` event from the Adapter's four-way read (CT-45) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
735	| `SNAP_SECTOR_DEG` | float, deg | 60-120, default 90 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | the width of the primary sector |
736	| `dist` | float, layout px | >= 0 | calculated | used **only for ordering and never displayed** (WM:1049, ASK-AD-7) |
737	| `ordinal(c)` | int | 1..N | `chart_layout.json` | stable authored ordinal, the last tie-break |
738	
739	**Output Range:** a node in `F` or "stay"; no wrap, no shake, no flash. The half-open interval `[-half, +half)` puts a node exactly on a diagonal in **exactly one** sector (45 degrees belongs to up, not right; 315 degrees belongs to right, not down), so the result is deterministic. `delta` is rounded to four decimals before the comparison so a floating-point 44.99999999 does not decide a diagonal. Content-lint invariant: the snap graph over the authored layout is strongly connected (every focusable node reachable from every other in at most `N - 1` presses).
740	
741	**Example** (illustrative data, not authored content; screen coordinates, y down): HOME (144, 100), A (210, 60), B (80, 40), `SNAP_SECTOR_DEG = 90`. Focus HOME, press right (theta 0): A has d = (66, 40), phi = 31.2, delta = 31.2, in `S1`; B has d = (-64, 60), phi = 136.9, delta = 136.9, out; result **A**. Press up (theta 90): A delta = -58.8, B delta = +46.9, both outside [-45, 45), so `S1` is empty; `S2` admits both (|delta| < 90); distances HOME-A 77.2 and HOME-B 87.7; result **A** (this is why the fallback exists: with three authored points, up from HOME would otherwise be a dead control). Press left (theta 180): B delta = -43.1, in `S1`; result **B**. Press down (theta 270): A delta = 121.2, B delta = -133.1, both outside 90, `S2` is empty: **focus stays** (no wrap). From A, press left: HOME delta = 31.2, result HOME. Stick navigation is edge-triggered at the Controller's deadzone with the repeat schedule of D.9.

765	### D.5 Filament drift
766	
767	The filament drift formula is defined as:
768	
769	`r = FILAMENT_DRIFT_FRACTION * V_DRIFT_CEIL; mean_us = round(1000000 * FILAMENT_DRIFT_STEP_PX / r); interval_us(i) = max(STEP_MIN_GAP_S * 1000000, (DRIFT_STEP_INTERVAL_PM[i mod 7] * mean_us) div 1000), with STEP_MIN_GAP_S = FILAMENT_DRIFT_STEP_PX / V_DRIFT_CEIL; each UI frame while r_eff > 0: acc_us += min(dt_us, UI_DT_MAX_MS * 1000); if acc_us >= interval_us(i) then one step is applied (n_applied += 1; i += 1; acc_us := 0), at most one applied step per frame; under reduced motion r_eff = 0 and acc_us, i and n_applied hold; offset_px = FILAMENT_DRIFT_STEP_PX * n_applied mod P_f; the offset is applied to the ring-1 filament sheet only` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, G2: creative-director lean, authored irregular step table)* (replaces the three step generators, the gap filter and its pending queue: the mechanism was over-engineered for a 0.5 px/s background that only has to never read as a pulse; the ceiling now holds by construction because every applied interval is floored at `STEP_MIN_GAP_S`)

777	| `FILAMENT_DRIFT_STEP_PX` | int, art px | 1-2, default 1 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | the quantum, so the texture never sits on a half pixel |
778	| `acc_us`, `i` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | int microseconds, int | 0 up; persist across opens | this layer (CT-43) | the step timer and the table index; they hold under reduced motion and do not rewind on re-open (they replace the three accumulators `a_k`) |

Over 72,000 frames: 85 whole cycles (595 steps, 71,400 frames) plus 600 frames (steps at 168, 240, 378 and 474) = **599** steps. At fraction 1.0: `mean_us` = 1,000,000 and the intervals are 1,400, 1,000 (the 600 entry is floored), 1,150, 1,000 (floored), 1,250, 1,000 (floored) and 1,100 ms, so no two steps are less than 60 frames apart and any rolling 1-s window holds at most one applied step. Reduced motion switched on at 100 s holds the timer, the index and the offset for as long as the toggle stays on; switched off it resumes from the held `acc_us`. A 400 ms hitch frame is clamped to 50 ms and adds 50 ms (2.5 % of the 2,000 ms mean interval) to `acc_us`, not 400 ms, and applies at most one step.
788	
789	### D.6 Depth-ring ground steps
790	
791	The depth-ring tone formula is defined as:
792	
793	`tone(i, c) = G(c) - ((2 * (G(c) - V(c)) * i + CHART_RING_STEPS) div (2 * CHART_RING_STEPS)) for i in 0 .. CHART_RING_STEPS and each channel c; ring i + 1 is band i for i < CHART_RING_STEPS; the centre disc is i = CHART_RING_STEPS; ordering contract: for every i and c, tone(i, c) - tone(i + 1, c) >= RING_STEP_MIN_CHANNEL`
794	
795	**Variables:**
796	
797	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
798	|---|---|---|---|---|
799	| `G(c)` | int, 8-bit channel | (28, 33, 40) = Ground `#1C2128` | ART 4.1, 4.6 (cited) | ring 1, where every MVP node sits |
800	| `V(c)` | int, 8-bit channel | (11, 16, 24) = Void Steel `#0B1018` | ART 4.1, 4.6 (cited) | the centre disc, exactly |
801	| `CHART_RING_STEPS` | int | 1-5 by the contract (the span of 16 units allows `floor(16 / 3) = 5`); default 3, MVP content ceiling 3 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | the number of ring bands drawn |
802	| `RING_STEP_MIN_CHANNEL` | int, 8-bit units | 2-6, default 3 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD (art-director ruling 5.1, checkpoint ruling Q5) | the minimum per-channel step so adjacent steps survive 8-bit quantisation and a poor panel |
803	
804	**Output Range:** each tone lies between Ground and Void Steel and the sequence is strictly darker inward; the disc equals Void Steel exactly. The formula is the **ordering contract made concrete**: it restates no percentage (ART 7.4 and WM:1050 say "about 4 %", which cannot be satisfied together with "reaches Void Steel"; conflict row C16, routed to the art-bible owner). The tones are derived values, never new palette entries and never registered (R16, R28).
805	
806	**Example** (`CHART_RING_STEPS = 3`, Ground (28, 33, 40), Void Steel (11, 16, 24)): ring 1 (i = 0) = (28, 33, 40) `#1C2128`; ring 2 (i = 1) = (22, 27, 35) `#161B23`; ring 3 (i = 2) = (17, 22, 29) `#11161D`; centre disc (i = 3) = (11, 16, 24) `#0B1018`. Per-channel steps are 6/6/5, 5/5/6 and 6/6/5, minimum 5 >= `RING_STEP_MIN_CHANNEL` 3, so the contract holds with margin. The art-director's illustrative tones (24, 29, 36), (20, 25, 32), (15, 20, 28) in the art-director's proposal are one evenly-divided reading over four intervals; the checkpoint ruling (Q5) fixed ring 1 = Ground exactly, so this interpolation governs and the exact on-screen values are verified in the spike (banding check by pixel sampling, AC-CT-47).
807	
808	### D.7 Newest-record line
809	
810	The newest-record line formula (main-menu Continue line only; read on every `MAIN_MENU` entry (re-read after a FAULTED return, a failed `new_game` or a Display & Comfort return, TX-34, TX-37; never refreshed while the menu stays open) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the pause panel carries no save fact, CT-17) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* is defined as:
811	
812	`HH = playtime div 3600; MM = (playtime mod 3600) div 60; SS = playtime mod 60; text = zero-pad(HH, 2) + ":" + zero-pad(MM, 2) + ":" + zero-pad(SS, 2)`
813	
814	**Variables:**
815	
816	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
817	|---|---|---|---|---|
818	| `playtime` | int, seconds | >= 0 | Save/Load `SaveInfo.playtime` (`T div TICK_RATE`, whole seconds; read as given, never recomputed here) | the playtime of the newest generation, read on every `MAIN_MENU` entry (re-read after a FAULTED return, a failed `new_game` or a Display & Comfort return, TX-34, TX-37; never refreshed while the menu stays open) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* for the main-menu Continue line *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
819	
820	**Output Range:** `HH` grows past two digits without wrapping ("100:00:00" for 360,000 s); the string is set in the instrument face with tabular numerals; it is static while the Continue screen is open (no tick, no "time since"); no wall clock enters. **Width term** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `W_line = n_chars * ADV_INST_HUD`, with `ADV_INST_HUD` = 6 HUD px for the 7-px-cap face and 4 for the 5-px-cap face (`[UNV]`, estimates until the bitmap faces exist; `n_chars` = digits plus two colons, 8 for under 100 h, 9 for 100 to 999 h, 10 beyond). The 7-px face is used when `W_line <= content_w` of the host column; otherwise the 5-px face is used, and the lint asserts `10 * 4 = 40 <= content_w` at every row (56 at rows 4 and 6, so a 1,000-hour record still fits at the smallest canvas); a string is never truncated or wrapped.
821	
822	**Example.** `playtime = 9641`: `HH = 2`, `MM = (9641 mod 3600) div 60 = 2441 div 60 = 40`, `SS = 41`, text `02:40:41`. `playtime = 0` gives `00:00:00`. `playtime = 59` gives `00:00:59`.
823	
824	### D.8 Label fit
825	
826	The label fit formula is defined as:
827	
828	`W_text(key, row) = ceil(n_chars(key) * ADV_EM * em_px * TEXT_EXPANSION_TEST); a LABEL_1 key passes iff W_text <= content_w(row) * H(row); a LABEL_2 key passes iff the greedy word-wrap of its words at W_line = content_w(row) * H(row) gives at most two lines (a word is placed on the current line while the running width plus one space advance plus the word's width is at most W_line, else it starts a new line; a single word wider than W_line fails); a key that would need three lines fails` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (the earlier total-width test `W_text <= 2 * W_line` passed keys that cannot wrap, for example three words of 200 screen px at a 336 px line: total 626 <= 672, but the greedy wrap gives three lines)
829	
830	**Variables:**
831	
832	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
833	|---|---|---|---|---|
834	| `n_chars` | int | 1-80 | the `ct.*` key's string | the rendered character count of the whole key |
835	| `ADV_EM` | float | 0.5 (estimated) | **NOT SOURCEABLE** until the real reading face is imported | the average glyph advance as a fraction of the font size; the lint replaces `n_chars * ADV_EM * em_px` with the measured width of the real face at each row |
836	| `em_px` | int, screen px | the ART 7.1 menu-body floor | ART 7.1 (cited, 1080p and 1440p only; sub-1080p floors are ASK-UP-2 / OQ-CT-13) | the font size of panel labels (reading face, CT-17) |
837	| `TEXT_EXPANSION_TEST` | float | 1.2-1.5, default 1.3 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | the localisation growth factor the lint applies to every key |
838	| `content_w`, `H` | int | D.1 | D.1 | the width available and the HUD scale of the row |
839	
840	**Output Range:** pass or fail per key per row; a failing `LABEL_1` fails the build (a label is never truncated or ellipsised at runtime, CT-28).
841	
842	**Example** (estimated advance, flagged `[UNV]`). "Display & Comfort", 17 characters, at 20 px: `ceil(17 * 0.5 * 20 * 1.3) = 221 <= 336` (row 6 content width in screen px, registry `safe_margin` rounded up), so it fits one line at every row; "Save & Quit" gives 143. A 36-character label gives `468 > 336`: it fails `LABEL_1` at rows 3 to 6 (content widths 348 and 336 screen px) and passes `LABEL_2` only if its greedy wrap at 336 gives two lines (for two roughly equal halves of about 234 px it does) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. At 1440p (row 1 canvas, `H = 4`, `em_px` 26): `W_panel = 2560 div 12 = 213`, `content_w = 213 - 4 - 32 = 177` HUD px = 708 screen px, and "Display & Comfort" needs `ceil(17 * 0.5 * 26 * 1.3) = 288`.
843	
844	### D.9 Directional-navigation repeat
845	
846	The navigation repeat formula is defined as:
847	
848	`n_moves(t_held) = 1 if t_held < UI_NAV_REPEAT_MS else 1 + floor((t_held - UI_NAV_REPEAT_MS) / UI_NAV_REPEAT_RATE_MS) + 1; a move past the last node in the pressed direction is a no-op (no wrap); a direction edge is taken only after the stick passes MOVE_DEADZONE and is released only below MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`
849	
850	**Variables:**
851	
852	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
853	|---|---|---|---|---|
854	| `t_held` | int, ms of UI process time | >= 0 | this layer (CT-43) | how long the direction has been held since its edge |
855	| `UI_NAV_REPEAT_MS` | int, ms | 250-500, default 350 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | the delay before auto-repeat starts |
856	| `UI_NAV_REPEAT_RATE_MS` | int, ms | 80-200, default 120 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | the interval between repeats |
857	| `MOVE_DEADZONE`, `MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT` | float | Controller values | PCI, not registered (cited) | the hysteresis that stops a stick on the boundary from chattering; **applied by the Adapter** before it publishes `NAV_DOWN` / `NAV_UP` (CT-45), not by this layer *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
858	
859	**Output Range:** `n_moves` >= 1 once the edge is taken; a key or d-pad press uses the same schedule. **One move per frame** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: a frame applies at most one move, and a repeat that is due but not yet applied is dropped, never queued, so a hitch frame cannot move focus twice; the clamp `UI_DT_MAX_MS` (D.2) is constrained to `UI_DT_MAX_MS <= UI_NAV_REPEAT_RATE_MS` (C-9) so one clamped frame can make at most one repeat due.
860	
861	**Example.** Held for 1,000 ms with 350 / 120: moves at 0, 350, 470, 590, 710, 830, 950 ms, so `n_moves = 1 + floor(650 / 120) + 1 = 1 + 5 + 1 = 7`. Held for 300 ms: 1. A 400 ms hitch frame during the hold is clamped to 50 ms and applies at most one move (not three) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
862	
863	### D.10 Layer-3 draw-call estimate
864	
865	The layer-3 draw-call estimate formula is defined as:
866	
867	`D_L3 = (CHART_RING_STEPS + 1) + D_filament + 3 * N_nodes + D_pod + D_route + D_seam + D_frame + D_text + D_hints + D_bracket; D_L3 <= LAYER3_DRAW_CALL_BUDGET` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: each node now costs a Ground clearing, a glyph and at most a tick, 3 calls; layer 2 is hidden under a full-bleed plate)*
868	
869	**Variables:**
870	
871	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
872	|---|---|---|---|---|
873	| `D_filament` | int | 3 | art-director assets A6 and A7 | the drifting sheet (ring 1; one sheet stepped by the authored interval table, D.5) plus the two static sheets |
874	| `D_L3` | int | about 20-35 on the chart *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | calculated | layer-3 draw calls while the chart is open |
875	| `CHART_RING_STEPS` | int | 1-5, default 3 | D.6, Tuning Knobs | ring bands; `+ 1` adds the centre disc |
876	| `N_nodes` | int | 3 at MVP | `web.view` | HOME plus two derelicts; each costs a Ground clearing, a glyph and, at most, a tick (3 calls); a berthed or absorbed record is a node drawn at its attach point (CT-11) |
877	| `D_pod`, `D_route`, `D_frame` | int | 0-1 each | CT-11 | pod marker, dashed route (one tiled quad), border and rivets |
878	| `D_seam` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | int | 0-2 | CT-11 | the berth seam quad (0-1) plus one Ground erase quad per ABSORBED record on the chart (0-2 at MVP; the sum is at most 2) |
879	| `D_bracket` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | int | 1 on the spatial chart (a focused node always exists), 0 otherwise | CT-6 | the bracket and bezel thickening, one draw |
880	| `D_text`, `D_hints` | int | 0-1 / 0-8 | CT-15, CT-28 | the `IN TRANSIT` word; control hints, **two draws per hint (one keycap glyph, one label run)** for 0-4 hints, so up to 8 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
881	| `LAYER3_DRAW_CALL_BUDGET` | int | default 40 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 30-60, and at least `D_L3` at the configured `CHART_RING_STEPS` and `N_nodes` (load-time assert, Tuning Knobs coupled constraint C-5) | this GDD; the Pipeline now carries the `D_L3` term in `D_root` (D.8 and D.16, ASK-CT-12 answered) | the cap *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: a number is set)* |
882	
883	**Output Range** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-stated in the re-review for the bracket, the seam term and two-draw hints)*: about 20 to 35 calls on the chart (26 in the MVP example; at most 33 at `CHART_RING_STEPS` 5, three nodes, a seam and an erase quad, the `IN TRANSIT` word and the maximum four hints); fewer on the panel (a plate, four items, a bracket, a status slot). **Example:** 4 ring fills + 3 sheets + 9 node calls (clearing, glyph, tick for each of three nodes) + 1 pod + 1 route + 0 seam + 1 frame + 0 text + 6 hint draws (3 hints x 2) + 1 bracket = 26 <= 40 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (was 22; the bracket and the two-draw hints were missing). **Maximum:** 6 ring fills + 3 sheets + 9 + 1 + 1 + 2 seam + 1 + 1 text + 8 + 1 = 33 <= 40. This is an **estimate**: batching can lower it, and the Pipeline measures the real figure per viewport with `Viewport.get_render_info(RENDER_INFO_TYPE_CANVAS, ...)` (PIPE D.8, AC-CT-45). **Layer 2 under the open layer (OQ-CT-16 closed):** the HUD (layer 2) is **hidden at MVP while a full-bleed plate is open** (`CHART`, `CHART_VIEW_ONLY`, `UI3_PLATE`), because an opaque plate covers it entirely (CT-3) and the draws would be wasted; with the panel open it stays drawn, frozen and undimmed beside the panel (an active warning mark held ON, HS-23). `D_L3` therefore excludes `D_hud` on a full-bleed plate. In OVERLAY (VS-B) the HUD critical strip must stay above layer 3 (the ADR (b) constraint: the opaque panel must never cover the critical strip, only the hand rail, R-AD-6). The Pipeline now carries the layer-3 term (`D_root = D_hud + D_filter + D_hold + D_L3`, PIPE D.8 and D.16), which answers ASK-CT-12; the hiding of layer 2 is a request to the Pipeline owner (ASK-CT-12b).

903	## Edge Cases
904	
905	Format: **If [condition]**: [exact outcome]. [rationale]. Ids are `EC-CT-n` and are cited by the acceptance criteria. "SOLO" and "OVERLAY" are the two `PauseGate` modes (CT-4); a sentence that names neither holds in both. Where an outcome depends on a neighbour that has not decided, it is marked provisional and points at the ask or open question.
906	
907	### A. The pick and the target
908	
909	- **EC-CT-1. If the picked record becomes ABSORBED, ORPHAN or `berthed`, or disappears from `web.view`, while the chart is open**: `ChartPick := NONE` on that `web.view` change, the dashed line disappears in the same frame, the bracket stays where it is, and if the node holding key or pad focus left the focusable set, focus moves to HOME; no message is shown. A stale pick is the only way the chart and the console press can disagree (CT-8).
910	- **EC-CT-2. If a `request_restore` completes while any state of the layer is open (any `restore_reason`)**: the layer closes into `CLOSED` in the same frame with no animation (TX-27), `ChartPick := NONE`, and the machine is rebuilt from CLOSED. The restored world may not contain the record that was picked, and nothing about the layer is in a snapshot (CT-27).
911	- **EC-CT-3. If the pod console is pressed at HOME with no valid pick and exactly one legal target exists** (POD or DOCK prompt with nothing berthed, CT-10 R3 and R4b): the chart opens with focus on HOME; no hop, no refusal, no simulation effect (SOLO also requests the pause, CT-4, as a governed raise, CT-3). An auto-implied hop would make one press both the choice and the commitment (CT-10; WM:1225) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
912	- **EC-CT-4. If the pod console is pressed while the pod is at a derelict**: HOME is implied and the hop proceeds with no chart involvement; the pick is not read. If the chart is open instead, HOME is the only focusable node, the dashed line runs from the pod's node to HOME, accept on HOME does nothing and `ChartPick` stays NONE. The only legal move needs no choice (WM-4, WM-8; CT-10).
913	- **EC-CT-5. If accept lands on the already-picked node, on HOME while the pod is at HOME, or on a non-selectable node**: the picked node stays picked (idempotent); HOME clears the pick; a non-selectable node (ORPHAN, `berthed`) does nothing. A double press must never clear a pick by accident (CT-7).
914	- **EC-CT-6. If the picked record changes status on the same presentation frame as the console press**: the Adapter injects whatever the pick held when the press was processed, and Web Map & Transit's own reasons decide (`TARGET_ABSORBED`, `TARGET_BERTHED`, `TARGET_UNKNOWN`), shown as words on the register plate by Interaction. The chart never re-validates a command; it only mirrors selectability (CT-9).
915	- **EC-CT-7. If every derelict is ABSORBED or ORPHAN (the legal set is empty)**: the chart opens with HOME as the only focusable node, no message, no "all charted" line; a no-pick console press still opens the chart. There is no completion state and no win state (anti-pillar; WM guard rail 5).
916	- **EC-CT-8. If an unwelded derelict B is `berthed` and the player opens the chart** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `legal_targets` is `{}` (CT-9), so no derelict can be picked (the earlier "A stays selectable" is retired); a stale pick made before the berthing is invalidated by CT-8 and its route removed; a POD press at the console is answered in Web Map's `BERTH_PENDING` words and opens no chart (CT-10 R6). The mirror reads only the `berthed` field and does not copy WM-9's reason order (CT-9; OQ-CT-3).
917	- **EC-CT-9. If a fuel level, a hop timer or any other Graph value changes while the chart is open**: selectability, focus and drawing are unchanged. The mirror never reads `FUEL_LOW`, `BUSY`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `NOT_LIT`, `ARRIVAL_BLOCKED` or `CAPACITY`; it reads the `berthed` field, and the empty set while a record is `berthed` and not ABSORBED is the whole of its `BERTH_PENDING` reflection (CT-9, D.4 Output Range) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G4)*; a fuel-dependent greying would be a fuel meter on the truth layer (CT-9, CT-35; AC-CT-24).
918	- **EC-CT-80. If a derelict B is berthed and the DOCK prompt is pressed while `ChartPick` holds A (or any value)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the press is `unberth{}` (CT-10 R5); the pick is not read, not injected and not cleared, and the chart does not open. Before this rule, rule 3 ("no valid pick opens the chart") could swallow an unberth press, which would have trapped a berthed-but-never-welded pod (WM-22).
919	- **EC-CT-81. If the chart was opened by a console press and the player presses `cancel`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the layer returns to `CLOSED` and SOLO resumes (TX-35), not to a `PANEL` the player never opened; `chart_table` also closes (TX-15). Opened from the panel, `cancel` returns to the panel (TX-19). The entry origin is host-local and is lost on any restore (TX-27).
920	
921	### B. Pause, input and focus
922	
923	- **EC-CT-10. If Esc (or Start) is held and key echo arrives**: only the first non-echo press toggles the layer; the Adapter suppresses echoes (CT-45) so the layer never sees them. A held Esc must not flicker the layer open and shut (CT-41(3); key-echo detection is NOT SOURCEABLE in the engine reference, ADR candidate (e)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
924	- **EC-CT-11. If `chart_table`, `cancel`, release, pointer exit or window focus loss occurs during a hold-to-confirm fill**: the bar snaps to empty in the same frame and nothing else happens; a second `chart_table` press then closes the layer. One press must not abort a destructive gesture and also resume the simulation (CT-5, CT-22, TX-10).
925	- **EC-CT-12. If `chart_table` and `cancel` arrive on the same frame**: they are processed in that order, `chart_table` closes the whole layer, and the `cancel` is consumed with nothing to step back to. One frame, one effect (CT-5).
926	- **EC-CT-13. If `chart_table` is pressed twice inside one tick boundary (SOLO)**: the layer's own `open` boolean toggles twice and `PauseGate` re-issues the latest desired state until the kernel state matches, so the layer is never wedged half-open. Whether the kernel coalesces or executes a same-boundary `request_pause` and `request_resume` in order is ASK-CT-9; the layer needs only that it converges (CT-4).
927	- **EC-CT-14. If the last-used device switches mid-navigation**: glyphs swap after `DEVICE_SWITCH_HYSTERESIS`, key and pad focus is retained, the bracket hides on mouse motion and reappears on the next key or pad navigation (CT-6; PC-13). 1313	### Motion constraints
1314	
1315	**CT-VA-10. Authority.** ART 7.3, "Menus and chart table", quoted: *"Cuts and short fades (80-120 ms), no slides, no bounces, no parallax. The focus bracket snaps with a 100 ms ease-out. The web map's filaments drift at <= 1 art px s^-1 in the current ring only (2.11); everything human on the map is static. Hold-to-confirm (HR-14) fills a linear bar with a needle-mark, never a radial wipe (3.4). Sober means almost nothing moves, and what moves is the web."*
1316	
1317	**CT-VA-11. What moves (the complete list).** Everything else is static: nodes, silhouettes, glyphs, routes, seams, ring steps, rivets and text.
1318	
1319	| Moving thing | Rule | Clock |
1320	|---|---|---|
1321	| Filaments, **ring 1 only** | whole-art-px offsets (`FILAMENT_DRIFT_STEP_PX`), direction fixed per sheet, no oscillation, at `FILAMENT_DRIFT_FRACTION` of the cited ceiling (D.5) | the layer's own UI clock (CT-43); `present_time` is frozen under pause (PIPE:265) |

What never appears.** (1) **Settle, tremor, glide** (ART 7.3's three signatures) are readings only; a needle-like wander on any chart element would be read as the class-(b) glide (HR-5) and teach the player that the one honest layer lies. (2) No parallax between the ring plate and the filaments (ART 7.3). (3) No pulse on HOME, the unknown tick or the pod marker: a pulsing Tungsten point would be an Attention-style signal (P3) and an ETA proxy. (4) No scrolling drift of the whole map: the drift is a texture offset inside ring 1, not a camera. (5) No camera jolt (PR-3), no screen shake, no blur, no scale change under any state (HR-13). 1338	
1339	**CT-VA-14. Hold bar motion.** Linear fill, no easing, no overshoot, whole-art-px steps (a `L_BAR_HUD` 64 bar over `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` (0.8 s, the Player Controller's registry value at authoring, illustrative) advances 80 art px a second, about 1.3 art px a frame at 60 Hz: no stepping problem). The fill is a monotonic luminance rise confined to the bar, never full-frame, and runs once per hold, so it is well inside the 3 Hz ceiling (HR-13). The abort snap-to-empty is a single transition. The bar is **function, not decoration**, so reduced motion does not remove it (HR-8 spirit: keep information, drop ornament).

1341	**CT-VA-15. Flicker ceiling (HR-13, 3 Hz)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Every luminance transition on this layer is single-shot and bounded by 120 ms. The ceiling is the Pipeline's registry `flash_count` (`F <= FLASH_MAX_PER_S` = 3; a flash is one pair of opposing transitions of at least 0.10 relative luminance; `F = ceil(n_transitions / 2)` per PR-13 and D.15), evaluated over the **layer-3 rectangle and the frame mean** from a per-frame linear-luminance log, with the HUD warning-mark edges counted in the same capture; this GDD owns no second metric. The way to exceed it is repeated toggling of a whole plate (an Esc or Chart mash); the re-open governor of CT-3 bounds that at three raises per rolling second (one under reduce flashing). Rapid focus movement is not governed separately: the bracket changes a small area, is bounded by its 100 ms ease and is below the 10 % luminance step on the frame mean; the capture of AC-CT-115 includes a held-direction run to prove it. 1343	### Art rulings carried into the GDD
1344	
1345	**CT-VA-16. Depth steps are an ordering contract, not a percentage (clarification C16).** ART 7.4 and WM:1050 say each step is "about 4 % darker toward centre; the inner ring's centre reaches Void Steel". The arithmetic does not close: Ground `#1C2128` is (28, 33, 40) and Void Steel `#0B1018` is (11, 16, 24), a span of 17 / 17 / 16 units; 4 % relative is about 1.5 units a step (near-invisible after 8-bit quantisation, ART 8.11 flag 1, and it never reaches Void Steel), and 4 points of white overshoots below Void Steel. The governing reading is the **ordering contract of D.6**: ring 1 is Ground itself (the lightest, where every MVP node sits and every contrast check is measured), each ring band is darker than the one outside it by at least `RING_STEP_MIN_CHANNEL` per channel, and the centre disc is exactly Void Steel. **The D.6 interpolation governs: (28, 33, 40), (22, 27, 35), (17, 22, 29), (11, 16, 24).** The art-director's first illustrative tones (24, 29, 36), (20, 25, 32), (15, 20, 28) assumed ring 1 below Ground; checkpoint ruling Q5 fixed ring 1 = Ground exactly, so they are superseded and not live values. Exact on-screen values are verified by pixel sampling in the spike (AC-CT-47, banding check at 1080p and the Deck canvas). The "about 4 %" wording is not restated as a value in this GDD; the clarification is routed to the art-bible owner (C16). The tones are derived values, never new palette entries and never registered.
1346	
1347	**CT-VA-17. The `IN TRANSIT` word.** Inline on the full-bleed Ground, **no plate** (ART 7.4's register is already Ground). Instrument face (bitmap, 7 art px cap height), Paper White, tabular letterspacing of one art px (ART 7.1). **Fixed frame position**: inside the chamfered border at the top-left, anchored to the picture rect with the 5 % safe margin (PIPE:88); it is a status word like a label on a bezel and is never placed near the origin node, the target node or along the route, because position would read as direction or progress that `web.view` structurally lacks (WM-36). Shown iff `pod_at == IN_FLIGHT` (CT-15); it appears and disappears in a cut with the data; no ellipsis animation ("IN TRANSIT..."), no blinking, no dots. BERTHING shows **no word and no element** (WM:1307). The word is the only text on the chart during flight: there is no "arriving in" and no counter.

The planned-sortie relation is a Tungsten dashed rule beneath the picked row (1 art px, no new asset, no fill, no new colour). The `IN TRANSIT` word keeps its fixed top-left position. **List order is a ranking proxy** (a vertical list invites "top is best"), so it is the stable authored order of CT-44: HOME first, derelicts in layout-file order, never sorted; this is acceptance criterion AC-CT-31. Rows are never truncated; if a list cannot fit, the canvas minimum was mis-set.
1350	
1351	**CT-VA-19. Filaments and rings: authored (D12), three bands (D20).** (1) Authored, not procedural: ART 3.4 requires branching, non-repeating, no right angles, density rising inward, which is hand-drawn art direction; procedural generation is a VS-A candidate to be revisited only if ring 2-3 content arrives. For MVP: one hand-authored filament sheet for ring 1 (drifting, scrolling by whole-art-px offset with a seamless wrap that creates no visible seam or repeat at any reachable canvas; the sheet is longer than the largest canvas in the drift axis plus one wrap period) and static sheets for the horizon bands. (2) Three bands plus the Void Steel centre disc give the "inward-pulling" composition (ART 2.11) and the Depth Rings of the Vertical Slice then need no layout change. Rings 2 and 3 are horizon only, with static filaments denser toward the centre (ART 3.4), no nodes, no labels, no ticks. (3) Ring 1 is the sparsest band, so the drifting filaments are the sparsest: correct for "very low energy" (ART 2.11).
1352	
1353	**CT-VA-20. Route and dash grammar.** The planned sortie is Tungsten, dashed, 1 art px, dash 2 on / 2 off art px (`ROUTE_DASH`, `[PLACEHOLDER]`), rectilinear segments only (human geometry over inhuman, ART 3.4). ART 7.4 also lists "routes dashed Hull Grey", but the MVP star topology has no standing routes, so the planned sortie is the only route drawn; if non-planned routes ever land (Hull Grey) they must use a different dash pattern, because the Tungsten versus Hull Grey distinction alone is weak in greyscale (shape backup, ART 4.0 principle 2). C12 is closed by Web Map & Transit (`leg_target_id`, `leg_dir`): the in-flight route is drawn on an OUT leg only, from those fields; on a BACK leg it is absent and the word `IN TRANSIT` remains alone (CT-15). Routes, seams and rivet lines are **textured quads of a 1-art-px tile**, not width-1 line draws (the 4.7 `CanvasItem` line draw has no antialiasing feather) -> ADR candidate (b), the layer-3 component library.

1355	**CT-VA-21. Main-menu backdrop.** The main menu and the boot-flow screens reuse the depth-step plate and the ring-1 filament sheet as their Ground backdrop with **no nodes** (a node would imply a save state or leak a Continue fact), the menu column sitting left of the centre disc so the composition still pulls the eye inward behind the list. Fallback if the playtest finds it noisy: plain Ground. No title art, no logo animation, no tagline (anti-pillar: no authored story). A game title, if shown, is a reading-face title (title floor of ART 7.1), Paper White.

1358	
1359	**CT-VA-22. Faces and localisation.** **Instrument face** (bitmap, 7 px and 5 px cap, integer `H`): labels, `IN TRANSIT`, the main-menu Continue numerals, `FAILED`, keycap letters (no node labels at MVP). **Reading face** (vector humanist sans; regular plus one heavier weight, no light weights): settings copy, notices, messages, list item labels in menus, titles. Floors are cited from ART 7.1, not restated (Tuning Knobs, cited rows). Both faces carry tabular numerals, a slashed or dotted zero and a distinct 1 / l / I. The bitmap set is a **closed list** (`IN TRANSIT`, digits, `FAILED`, short labels; CT-28; `RISKY` removed 2026-10-27, user rulings, D82): every sentence and any string likely to localise goes in the reading face, otherwise each locale needs hand-drawn bitmap glyphs (R-AD-10). The reading-face scale is continuous (the only non-integer text), so plates are sized to text with a minimum, not text fitted to a fixed plate; a reading-face line is 45-75 characters (ART 7.1); all text sits on an opaque Ground plate (HR-2). Chamfers only, no rounded corners (ART 3.4); one rivet per corner of the border, never as texture; dial arcs absent. Layout is anchored to the picture rect with the 5 % safe margin at every reachable canvas (CT-16). The right-third panel is `W_panel` HUD px wide (D.1); at row 6 it is 71 art px, so labels must fit by reading-face scale or compact behaviour applies: no label is truncated and none carries an ellipsis (CT-28).

1361	### Audio
1362	
1363	**CT-VA-23. Audio: requests only; the mood the visuals set.** The layer owns and specifies no sound (CT-29, rulings R26). It requests from Adaptive Audio a UI-bus focus-move cue, a confirm cue and the queued-re-open acknowledgement `UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED` (CT-3) (AA:562); nothing for open, save or load; `UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED` is one-shot, on the `ui` bus, with no visual twin, no sanity-stage or Attention dependence, and identical at `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` 334 and `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS_REDUCED` 1000; the Chart Table requests it on the press frame that puts a raise into the empty re-open queue, or replaces the queued raise with a different desired raise, once per queued raise; it is SILENT for an idempotent repeat of the same desired raise, for `cancel` of the queue, for the frame on which the queue applies the raise (the plate is the feedback), for a raise that applies at once (no lower within the interval) and for a `request_restore` that clears the queue (TX-27) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G2/G6: CT-3 queued acknowledgement, ASK-CT-20)*; no request depends on sanity stage or Attention (AA:562 "no sanity or Attention effect on menu audio", HR-6). Silent menus are acceptable at MVP. The visual mood the audio should match: **hush**. The chart table is the quietest room in the game, a place where nothing is wrong and nothing is being measured; menu and map audio should sit outside the fiction's danger. The one living thing is the slow drift of the web: if audio acknowledges it at all it is as a faint, constant, non-reactive bed, never a response to a chart action. Layers, ducking, fades and triggers remain the audio-director's (provisional — Adaptive Audio owns the cues).

1430	
1431	### Feel statement
1432	
1433	**CT-GF-1. The feel in one line.** Instant to answer, slow to move, never excited. Every input is answered in the frame it arrives or in the one after; nothing on the layer overshoots, bounces, pulses, shakes, glints or counts down (the three reading motions of ART 7.3 are absent, CT-2); the only autonomous motion is a web drifting at a fraction of one art pixel a second. The pause is a held breath, not a refuge (Player Fantasy, Moment 2): the panel appears without softening the world and disappears without ceremony.
1434	
1435	**CT-GF-2. Feel pillars for this layer.** (1) *Answered*: no input is ever swallowed without a visible or documented reason (a disabled item is shown disabled; `SAVE_QUIT_WAIT` ignores input by rule, CT-21). (2) *Held*: the world beneath is the same frame (PIPE:265), so the panel's arrival changes nothing it does not cover. (3) *Deliberate*: the irreversible acts (UI-3 quit, UI-5 retire and delete) cost a full hold *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* on a linear bar, and the sortie commitment is off this layer entirely (the console press, CT-10). (4) *Plain*: no easing except the 100 ms bracket, no sound beyond a focus-move cue, a confirm cue and the queued-re-open acknowledgement (CT-3) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G2/G6: CT-3 queued acknowledgement, ASK-CT-20)*.

1439	**CT-GF-3. Latency targets.** Frames are presentation frames of the root viewport; ticks are simulation ticks (`TICK_RATE` 60, so one tick is 16.67 ms). A target of "the same frame" means the first frame presented after the input event is processed.

1461	
1462	**CT-GF-4. Mash tolerance** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; replaces "every press is honoured, no cooldown")*. Every **close** is honoured on its press frame and there is no cooldown on any panel item (Resume, Display & Comfort, Save & Quit, Back). A **re-open** pressed within `CHART_REOPEN_MIN_MS` (334 ms; 1000 ms under reduce flashing) of the last close is latched and applied when the interval elapses, plate and kernel pause together, and only `cancel` cancels it; a repeat `chart_table` press is idempotent *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (CT-3 re-open governor, EC-CT-68, EC-CT-77 to 79). The feel is therefore: closing is instant, opening after a recent close can lag by up to a third of a second (a press that is queued and then cancelled with `cancel` has no on-screen effect at all, which a tester must not file as a swallowed input; the queued press itself gives an audio-only acknowledgement, ASK-CT-20) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, never both a plate and a running sim wrongly, and ten presses in one second never produce more than three raises (at most six opposing transitions, `F <= 3` under registry `flash_count`; AC-CT-114, AC-CT-115). A same-boundary press pair converges (`PauseGate` re-issues the latest desired state, EC-CT-13); `chart_table` held with key echo toggles exactly once (EC-CT-10; the Adapter suppresses echo, CT-45).
1463	
1464	**CT-GF-5. Input hygiene as feel.** The irreversible press is protected by feel rules, not by dialogs: a console press that opens the chart cannot also activate something (fresh press edge, CT-41 (1)); the `interact` that closes the layer on Resume is swallowed so the player standing at the pod console does not hop the instant they resume (CT-41 (2)); a click on the frozen world does nothing (CT-41 (4)); a held Esc does not flicker (CT-41 (3)). The player should never feel that the layer "did something I did not ask".

1484	**CT-GF-7. Snap targets (positions are always whole pixels).** (1) Every layer-3 rectangle is positioned by anchors 0 or 1 plus integer HUD-px offsets (CT-16), so every bezel, bracket and rivet edge lies on a screen-pixel boundary at every `H`; a centred element is allowed only at an even on-screen width. (2) Panel edge: `W_panel` HUD px, `W_panel * H` screen px, an integer by construction, so the panel's left edge `P_w - W_panel * H` is an integer screen pixel (D.1: 1281, 1284, 854, 854, 854, 854 for the six canvas rows). (3) Node positions: authored integers in the 288 x 162 frame, scaled by the integer `m` (D.1b); a 24x24 glyph stays 24x24 at `H`. (4) The bracket relocates between integer positions; during the 100 ms ease its interpolated draw positions are rounded to whole HUD px so the bracket never sits on a half pixel. (5) Hold bar needle: `needle_px = min(floor(fill * L_BAR_HUD), L_BAR_HUD - 1)` whole HUD px (D.2); a `L_BAR_HUD` 64 bar over `CONFIRM_HOLD_S` (0.8 s, the Player Controller's registry value at authoring, illustrative) advances 80 art px a second, about 1.3 px a frame at 60 fps. (6) Filaments: whole-art-px offsets only, so the texture never rests on a half pixel (D.5). (7) Routes, seams and rule lines: 1-art-px quads aligned to whole art px, never width-1 line draws on a fractional transform (CT-11).
1485	
1486	**CT-GF-8. Snap-to-node feel (gamepad and keyboard).** A direction press moves focus to the nearest focusable node whose bearing falls in the pressed direction's sector (`SNAP_SECTOR_DEG` 90 degrees), widening to the half-plane if the sector is empty, else staying (D.3). Feel targets: with three nodes, **no direction press is a dead control when another node exists on that side or in the half-plane** (the fallback exists for this); a press with no candidate leaves focus where it is with **no shake, no flash, no sound** (staying is silence, not an error); the bracket never wraps from the last node to the first; the same press always lands on the same node (deterministic, the diagonal assignment is exact, D.3); and every node is reachable from every other in at most N - 1 presses. Mouse and pad are equivalent in outcome: a click on a node is focus plus accept (CT-6). A stick resting on the deadzone boundary produces one move per edge, not a chatter (D.9, `MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`).
1487	
1488	### Weight, juice and what is deliberately absent
1489	
1490	**CT-GF-9. No juice, by rule.** No squash, scale pop, overshoot, bounce, wobble, shake, flash, glow, pulse, particle, screen-space effect, parallax, slide or wipe on any element of this layer (ART 7.3, rulings R16, CT-2). The press acknowledgement is a one-frame Paper White hold on the label (CT-VA-7). A destructive action looks like every other item until its bar fills. A completed hold fires on the same frame the bar is full; there is no celebratory beat. This is not austerity for its own sake: ornament on the truth layer reads as the layer reacting, and a reacting layer reads as an instrument that can be fooled.
1491	
1492	**CT-GF-10. Stillness as weight.** The panel is a heavy opaque plate, chamfered and riveted (ART 7.4), that does not move once placed; the world beside it is a held frame, undimmed. The contrast (a still true plate beside a world frozen mid-lie at stage 3) is the feel the Player Fantasy aims at (Moment 2). The only life on the chart is the filament drift, kept deliberately below the art-bible ceiling so the screen reads "very low energy" (ART 2.11) and never "something is happening".
1493	
1494	**CT-GF-11. Silence and absence of reward.** No sound on open, save or load; the only cues requested are a UI-bus focus-move cue, a confirm cue and the audio-only queued-re-open acknowledgement `UI_CHART_REOPEN_QUEUED` (CT-3, CT-29), owned by Adaptive Audio *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G2/G6: CT-3 queued acknowledgement, ASK-CT-20)*. No "progress saved", no autosave mark, no completion flourish, no achievement toast, no tip on the black between menu and world (CT-36). Save & Quit's feel is *closing the log*: the items dim, the process ends.
1495	
1496	### Feel risks and playtest observables
1497	
1498	**CT-GF-12. What the playtest measures (all advisory, none a gameplay constant).**
1499	- `CHART_TO_PRESS_S`: the median seconds from the first chart open of a sortie to the console press; target 20 s, flag above 40 s as the friction signal that Esc, Chart, pick, Esc, walk, press is too long. The reserved remedy is a separate chart action owned by the Player Controller, **never** data on the chart (Player Fantasy, validation 2; AC-CT-80).
1500	- Whether the 100 ms bracket ease reads as responsive or laggy on a gamepad at the Deck's 60 Hz (the knob is cited from ART 7.3, not retuned here; a complaint is routed to the art bible).
1501	- Whether `FILAMENT_DRIFT_FRACTION` 0.5 reads alive or dead (the first knob likely to move; Tuning Knobs, interaction notes).
1502	- Whether the pause reads "held" and not "safe" (validation 3; AC-CT-106).
1503	- The count of console presses made with a stale pick (a pick the player no longer remembers), per tester, and whether the text-free pick echo on the console plate was noticed (CT-10 item 5, AC-CT-124); a count above zero in two testers routes to Interaction and the UX spec, never to a timer that clears the pick *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
1504	- Whether a re-open delayed by the governor (up to 334 ms; 1000 ms under reduce flashing) is noticed or felt as a swallowed press (CT-3, CT-GF-4); the remedy is the AC-CT-115 capture and the interval, never removing the governor *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
1505	- Whether the hold at the registry value reads deliberate or sticky (a Controller-owned constant and the Alpha two-tap option (PCI:835)).
1506	
1507	**CT-GF-13. Frame-time feel.** The layer must never be the cause of a visible hitch: the layout file is parsed at boot, not on open; the settings flush completes inside one frame (a few hundred bytes on the UI thread); per-frame work is the bracket tween, one accumulator or two and a handful of draw calls (D.10 estimates 26 in the MVP example and 33 at the maximum, against `LAYER3_DRAW_CALL_BUDGET` 40) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The numeric script-time budget is `[PLACEHOLDER]` and measured in a spike on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK (delegated ruling R12; AC-CT-45, AC-CT-81, ADVISORY until set). A large frame delta (a window drag, a display-mode change) is clamped to `UI_DT_MAX_MS` (50 ms) so no hold completes and no drift jumps from a hitch (EC-CT-58, D.2 example: a 400 ms frame advances a hold by 50 ms only).

Cross-checks.** The feel numbers above are consistent with: ART 7.3 (fade band, bracket, drift ceiling, linear bar); HR-8 and HR-13 (reduced motion, 3 Hz); D.2, D.5, D.9 (hold, drift, repeat); CT-43 (the UI clock, independent of the kernel state so the bar and the drift run while the kernel is `PAUSED`); PCI:656 as clarified in C15.

content.content:
### Save & Quit and window close

- **If a Save & Quit is requested while any bound seat is `DOWNED`**: nothing is written — `save_and_quit` returns `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`, `save_status` is unchanged, and shutdown proceeds after the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving"; Continue then restores the newest verified generation. Rationale: no file on disk may ever hold a `DOWNED` or `DEAD` seat; the death stub would have restored the same file within `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS`.
- **If a Save & Quit is requested while a seat is `DEAD`**: unreachable in the solo MVP (the stub fires on the `DEAD` tick); the clause exists for multi-seat futures. Rationale: SL-6.
- **If a Save & Quit is requested with only a soft condition closed (a tell, a breach phase, `CHANNELLING`, `STAGGERED`, `IN_POD`, a `CRITICAL` suit, an open self-inflicted breach)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the generation is written immediately and tagged `RISKY` with its `risky_cause`; inside the post-`DOWNED` refractory with a healthy suit it is written and is not `RISKY`. Rationale: refusing to quit traps the player; quitting without writing silently discards up to one interval.
- **If a Save & Quit finds the state hash equal to the newest generation's (same `T`, nothing changed)**: the write is skipped (`SL_QUIT_DEDUPED`) and shutdown proceeds. Rationale: a duplicate generation would only push a useful one out of the ring.
- **If the Save & Quit write fails or times out (`SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS`)**: the quit is held, `save_status` reads `FAILED`, the pause panel stays, and the player may retry or quit without saving by hold-to-confirm. Rationale: never silently lose progress; never trap the player.
- **If the window is closed while a write is in progress** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the quit waits up to `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` (frame-polled, SL-6), then **holds**: `save_status` reads `FAILED`, `quit_held` is published and the player leaves only through the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving"; the next open reconciles by the crash table (T-6). Rationale: one outcome for a failed or slow quit, the one SL-6 and AC-SL-45c already state; an exit after a timeout would silently discard up to one interval.
- **If the window is closed while the kernel is `PAUSED` under the open Chart Table (SOLO)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass)*: Save/Load's handler runs `save_and_quit()` from `PAUSED` (`PAUSED → SAVING → PAUSED`) under SL-6's rules, then `request_shutdown`; the Chart Table calls nothing (EC-CT-38). **On a boot-flow screen** nothing is written and the process ends through boot code (ASK-CT-11). Rationale: one save path, the same rules everywhere.
- **If a quit is requested while the kernel is `FAULTED`**: no write is attempted (K:151); the quit proceeds to the menu or shutdown. Rationale: the faulting session is never saved over an existing generation.
- **If the window is closed while a seat is `DOWNED`, while the kernel is `LOADING`, or while it is `SAVING`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `DOWNED` writes nothing and holds the close for the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving" (`SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`); `LOADING` defers the close intent until the kernel is `RUNNING` and then handles it as a `RUNNING` close; `SAVING` lets the in-flight job reach `WRITTEN` or `FAILED` and then dedupes against it or writes the `QUIT` generation (SL-6, close mechanism; AC-SL-44b). Rationale: every state has one answer and none of them is a silent exit.
- **If a Save & Quit is made while a Graph warning window is open** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the generation is written at once and tagged `RISKY`; Continue restores a fault with less than `W_MIN_WARNING_S` of its warning left. It is not clamped (a clamp would trap the player at the menu to protect a window they can see) and it is counted by metric M4. Rationale: SL-6.
| OQ-48 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | **Requests to the Chart Table owner.** (1) CT-17 puts the newest-record line on the pause panel; the review moves it to the main-menu Continue screen only (UI-2, UI-4), and the panel's content must be identical across autosave periods whether the gate is open or deferring (AC-SL-133); the `SAVE_FAILED` panel state keeps its `FAILED` flag for the player's own held quit. (2) Save/Load now publishes `quit_held`, and the Chart Table presents its hold-to-confirm when a window close is held (SL-6). content.content:
**WM-36 — `web.view`, the read view (provisional name).** *Rule.* One pure, side-effect-free read view with **true values only**; the Chart Table (designed, `chart-table-web-map-and-menus.md`) displays it and writes nothing.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `nodes[]` | per record: `derelict_id`, `template_id`, `kind`, `ring`, `world_slot`, `status`, `unknown_seen`, `loaded` (derived from the Graph's pure `section(section_id) -> {kind, dormant}` read, ASK-G1 accepted), `berthed` (derived) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `pod_at` | a record id, or IN_FLIGHT |
| `transit_state` | IDLE, LEG, ARRIVING, BERTHING |
| `destination_ready` | `transit_state == IDLE`, true from the `pod_settle` apply tick (WM-14) |
| `leg_target_id`, `leg_origin_id`, `leg_dir` | the persisted `target_id`, `origin_id` and `leg_dir` (OUT, BACK) while `transit_state` is LEG or ARRIVING, else NONE: the in-flight leg's two endpoint identities only, never a position, time or progress datum (ASK-CT-3, Chart Table C12). On an OUT leg the route is `leg_origin_id` (HOME) to `leg_target_id`; on a BACK leg it is `leg_origin_id` (the departure derelict) to HOME *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `leg_origin_id` added; it is persisted since the re-review, so a restore in a BACK leg can rebuild the astern hull)* |

There is **no fuel field** (fuel is the Graph's witness), no Attention field, no sanity field and **no progress datum of any kind** (no elapsed ticks, no remaining ticks, no `t0`, no `n`; `leg_target_id`, `leg_origin_id` and `leg_dir` are endpoint identity, not progress): guard rail 1 is therefore a structural guarantee of this read surface, not a promise (checkpoint 2026-10-26, C12). A test double reading `web.view` must find none of them. **The Audio-only read.** The Adaptive Audio bed (designed, AA-33) needs the leg's timing to fade its bed in and out. It gets it from the `POD_DEPARTED` payload (`t0` and `n`, WM-31) and, for a mid-leg restore, from a separate read `web.leg_timing()` (name confirmed by Adaptive Audio, CX-A19; designed, `adaptive-audio-and-tells.md`) that returns `{t0, n}` only while `transit_state == LEG` and is **not** part of `web.view`; the Chart Table's contract names `web.view` alone, so the Chart Table can never reach a progress datum, and presenting either as an ETA or progress element is a defect. *Cites.* ART 7.4. *Pillar.* P1, P3. *Decided.* contract for the Chart Table (designed; its Web Map row reads `web.view` only). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*

Suit's `locomotion_cap` is read by the Controller, not by Interaction. *The pod console (CONSOLE object class; Web Map & Transit, Designed — WM-8, WM-9; Chart Table, Web Map & Menus, ASK-CT-1).* Two CONSOLE subjects, told apart by Layout's `console_role` on the `subject_anchors` entry (ASK-CT-13, ANSWERED 2026-10-28), carry the declaration rows: the **POD_CONSOLE** class (role POD; every dock room) carries `pod_hop` (carry-admitted); the **DOCK_CONSOLE** class (role DOCK; the home airlock only) carries `unberth` (priority 1, `eligible` additionally requires Web Map's `berthed_present()`) and `berth` (priority 2, `eligible` additionally requires NOT `berthed_present()`), so `select_verb` (IA-5) remains a function of (class, tool, eligible) and the DOCK plate shows `unberth` while a record is berthed. All rows: bare hand, TAP, state-neutral `verb_name_key`, `eligible` = Web Map's `console_ready(role)`; noise unchanged (`berth` LOUD, one U_LOUD push at the berth apply by Interaction, `unberth` and `pod_hop` QUIET *(Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): D59, route 1)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*). Both subjects are lit-gated (IA-6). The console press is the only trigger; the Adapter injects the host-local `ChartPick` held by the Chart Table into `pod_hop` at the POD press and into `berth` at the DOCK press; a press needing a pick with none valid opens the chart (presentation; no command is submitted); `unberth` takes no payload and never opens the chart (Chart Table CT-10 R1 to R8). **Stale-pick echo (ASK-CT-14, ANSWERED 2026-10-28):** the POD and DOCK prompt plates carry a small text-free glyph slot filled from the Chart Table's host-local read `pick_glyph_key` (the node glyph the chart draws for the pick, or HOME's glyph at a derelict POD press, R1); no name, ordinal, distance or cost (IA-39 unchanged); no timer clears the pick. Refusals are Web Map's closed WM-9 reasons, shown as words on the Chart Table's register plate (WM:1029) — the Chart Table's presentation of Web Map's reasons, never an Interaction prompt or reason string (IA-39); the payload-less POD press at HOME with a derelict berthed is routed to Web Map and answers `BERTH_PENDING` (WM-9, CT-10 R6). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ASK-CT-13 / ASK-CT-14 accepted, delegated G6, GAP)* `pod_hop` (POD_CONSOLE) is carry-admitted (IA-28); `berth` and `unberth` (DOCK_CONSOLE) are not; all three stay lit-gated (IA-6). *Decides:* CR-16, PC-9, WM-8, WM-9.
