60	
61	**The crew member the player is here** is the navigator of WM's committed crossing (WM:59, "the navigator's authority and the passenger's exposure in one beat"). Web Map & Transit owns the exposure half (the leg). This GDD owns the authority half, and the authority is honest only because the table is mute about the price.
62	
63	**Framing alternatives considered** (Category UI: direct framing).
64	
65	| | Framing | What it centres | Verdict |
66	|---|---|---|---|
67	| **A** | **Direct: "The honest table."** A sober human instrument where the player picks, stops and leaves. Nothing on it lies; nothing on it helps more than the crew has earned | P1 truth by layer (ART 7.0 row 3), P5 inward composition, the navigator's authority (ART 2.11) | **Adopted** |
68	| B | "The navigator's bridge": plotting the web as a mastery fantasy; route planning as skill expression | route planning, comparative choice between targets | **Rejected as primary.** The MVP web is a star of at most one hop (WM-4); a plotting fantasy over three nodes either overpromises or pulls cost, distance and ETA data onto the chart to give the plotting something to chew on, which is guard rail G6 below. It also repeats the framing Web Map & Transit rejected for the same reason (WM:78). The *word* navigator is kept (ART 2.11); the *fantasy of plotting* is not |
69	| C | "The refuge": the menu layer as sanctuary, a warm decompression space between horrors | relief, emotional recovery | **Rejected.** ART 2.11 puts the table "inside its mood"; a refuge would dim or soften the world (ART 7.4 forbids it), invite a calming cue (a relief sting is a mood effect, and menu audio carries no sanity or Attention effect, AA:562) and in solo turn the pause into a sanity-recovery exploit by feel even though Sanity reads nothing from it. It contradicts P2: the tell is still there when you come back. It is also Submission, which the concept ranks as "deliberately absent" (CON:89) |
70	| D | Diegetic prop: a physical chart table the player walks to in the home-ship | a place to stand, embodiment | **Ruled out (CT-1).** A prop is a lit, lie-capable instrument (ART 7.0 row 1) and is unreachable on a sortie. Recorded so a later stage does not re-propose it as a fantasy upgrade; no in-world schematic console exists: the Controller's Adapter owns the `inspect_card` context and In-World Instruments owns the card's content and draws no schematic (IW-28, C4) |
71	
72	*Why A carries the concept's MDA ranking (CON:82-89):* Discovery (1) is delivered by the chart **growing only by looking** (the Tungsten tick appears only once the unknown was seen from the pod, ART 7.4; WM:85); Challenge (2) by the chart **withholding the price**, so the player must read the Graph's witnesses; Fantasy (4) by the navigator role and the home silhouette growing with each absorbed section (Moment 4). **"And also" test at system scale:** *it is a galaxy map, and also it only remembers what your crew has lit, and it will never tell you what the trip costs.* The second clause sparks the right question ("then how do I know?") and the answer is the world.
73	
74	### Pillars served (verbatim, then scope notes)
75	
76	> **Pillar 1: The World Never Lies.** "Pipes leak, frost forms, air hisses; the physical world is ground truth. Only instruments and perception can be wrong. [...] *Design test*: a hidden stat vs. a visibly leaking pipe → the pipe." (CON:208-221)
77	
78	Primary. The Chart Table serves P1 from the side most systems never touch: it is the one surface in the game that is **not part of the world and therefore cannot be an instrument** (ART 7.0 row 3: "Chart table (meta): nobody in the fiction ... can a reading lie? never"). P1 says only instruments and perception can be wrong; this layer is neither. Its job is to be true *and to say almost nothing*, so that the truth the player needs still has to be read off the pipe.
79	
80	> **Pillar 5: Deeper Is Richer, Loss Is Not Total.** "Risk and reward map to depth in the web. [...] *Design test*: safe farming vs. scarcity that pushes inward → scarcity." (CON:272-279)
81	
82	Served by composition, not data: the chart darkens toward the centre ("the horizon the game never lets you reach", ART 2.11 carried element) and carries no completion, percentage or win datum (WM guard rail 5, WM:144). **Scope note (carried from WM:53):** the Chart Table does **not** carry the failure contract's "never knowledge" half. The chart is drawn from `web.view`, which is WORLD-scope and rolls back on restore (WM-28); the pick resets on every restore (CT-8). Nothing in this GDD may be cited as evidence that knowledge survives a failure; the Knowledge Codex (VS) owns that, and its chart annotations are a reserved slot (CT-38).
83	
84	> **Pillar 3: The Web Watches.** "Attention is shown in the world (creaking, flicker, filament movement), never as a hidden meter." (CON:231-237)
85	
86	Served by absence. The pillar names "filament movement" as an in-world Attention sign, and the chart also draws moving filaments. That collision is the most likely way this layer becomes an Attention meter by accident, so it is a named guard (G5, CT-40): **the chart's filament drift is constant and is never modulated by Attention, depth, sanity, time in session or anything else.** "Depth rings are shown as place, not as attention" (AT:1373).
87	
88	> **Pillar 4: Sanity Rewrites Reality.** "**No lie is unfalsifiable**: the truth is always available through the physical world, a second instrument, a saner crewmate, the human channel, or time — and checking costs time, risk or trust. At least one channel of truth always remains." (CON:261-265)
89	
90	Served twice, and the two halves pull against each other (resolved in "Under hallucination" below): the layer **is** a channel of truth that always remains, and it must **not** become a free way to check a lie, because P4 requires that checking cost something.
91	
92	> **Pillar 2: Dread Before Chaos.** "Every breach is preceded by a tell a careful player could have perceived (sound, light, gauge drift, hull stress)." (CON:223-229)
93	
94	Served by keeping the commitment off the menu: the console press is the point of no return (WM:1225; CT-10), the pause is non-diegetic only (KRN CR-16), and the panel never dims, blurs or desaturates the world it freezes (ART 7.4; PIPE:265), so a tell that was on screen when the player pressed Esc is still on screen while they stand at the panel.
95	
96	### Emotional arc across a session at the table
97	
98	Session shape from CON:181-185. Final copy for every surface is the UX spec's and the narrative director's; the register is fixed under "Tone and language".
99	
100	| When | Surface | Target feeling | Must never feel like |
101	|---|---|---|---|
102	| Boot | Photosensitivity notice (CT-20), then main menu (CT-23) | *Plain care.* A notice that asks once and never nags | A legal wall, a splash screen, a countdown |
103	| Session start | Continue line: playtime, crew count, kind, `RING <n>` (SL UI-4, amended to drop `RISKY`, D82) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | *A ship's log, not a trophy case.* "This is where we were." | A save-slot gallery, a thumbnail, a "last played 3 days ago" nudge, a completion bar |
104	| Planning | Chart, the pick (CT-7, CT-9) | *Sober competence* (ART 2.11) | Shopping, routing software, a quest board |
105	| Mid-sortie pause | Panel over the frozen world (CT-3, CT-4) | *A held breath.* The world is paused in the middle of being itself | A safe room, a decompression chamber, a dimmed "you are safe now" scrim |
106	| Natural stop | Save & Quit (CT-21) | *Closing the log.* "Natural stop: the ship is stable again." (CON:184) | A reward, "progress saved!", an autosave flourish |
107	| Mid-crisis quit while DOWNED | Hold-to-confirm "quit without saving", "the newest autosave will be used" (SL UI-3) | *Plain honesty about the cost* | A death screen, "you died", a guilt line |
108	
109	### Anchor moments
110	
111	All four occur in the MVP slice (home-ship 5 / derelict A 4 / derelict B 5 compartments, LSG MVP slice; WM roster). Glyphs and colours are WM section 3 (WM:1036-1050) and ART 7.4, cited and not restated with new values.
112	
113	**Moment 1, "The table remembers what you lit" (first sortie; the Discovery payoff).** The cryo bay is stable. The player walks to the home pod console and presses with no pick. The console does not refuse: the chart opens (CT-10, "a press with no valid pick opens the chart"). Full-bleed Ground; concentric steps darkening inward (CT-13); one Tungsten point with a rectilinear Foundry silhouette for HOME; two plain Graphite-lit rectangles, bare, no labels, for derelicts A and B (UNSEEN, WM:1041; on the spatial map, which is the layout at every MVP canvas row at `H_default`, and in the compact layout only the CT-44 neutral ordinal appears, identical for UNSEEN and SEEN, a slot mark and not a name). Focus starts on HOME, not on a target, so focus is never a recommendation. The player snaps the bracket to A (CT-6); nothing appears beside it: no distance, no fuel, no name (CT-14, CT-35). Esc, resume, press. After the leg and the residual lamp (WM Moment 1), the next time the chart opens A is a Foundry silhouette with **one 1-art-px Tungsten tick** (WM:1043). *What the player learns:* the chart grows only by looking. It is a record of the crew's own eyes.
114	
115	**Moment 2, "Stopping the clock is not stopping the world" (solo pause mid-tell at low sanity; the P1 + P4 payoff).** In derelict B, sanity at stage 3, a scrubber gauge reads fixed while frost creeps along the floor (CON P4(b)). The 10-30 s tell has begun (P2). The player presses Esc. A short cut-fade (inside the ART 7.3 band) and the right-third panel is on Ground: Resume, Chart, Display & Comfort, Save & Quit, in Paper White, the same at stage 3 as at stage 0 (CT-2, HR-6). To the left, the world is frozen **undimmed**: the lying gauge still reads fixed, the frost is still frost, the violet fringe on the gauge rim is still there, held in one frame (PIPE:265). Nothing on the panel says anything about any of it. Resume: the tell continues from exactly where it stopped. *What the player learns:* the menu is a place to stand, not a way out. It holds the world still; it does not make it kinder.
116	
117	**Moment 3, "The log, not the trophy" (next evening, the main menu; the P5 tone payoff).** Boot, main menu. Continue carries one line of SIM facts as words: playtime, crew count, kind, `RING 1` (SL UI-4 as amended: no `RISKY`; CT-23) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. No thumbnail, no screenshot of the ship, no "you were here", no percentage. If the newest record was unreadable, one plain ship-log line says so and Continue proceeds from the one before (SL UI-7). *What the player learns:* the game keeps a log of where they were, the way a ship does, and it will not flatter them.
118	
119	**Moment 4, "The ship is drawn from your history" (after the weld; the Fantasy / Investment payoff).** Derelict B was berthed and its sections welded. On the chart B first abuts the home silhouette with a solid 1-px Hull Grey seam (berthed, WM:1044), and once absorbed it is drawn **as part of the home silhouette**, no tick (WM:1045). The home mark is now a different shape from the one in Moment 1. Nothing announces it; there is no "ship expanded" banner. The drawing rule that makes this visible is the home-ship composite of CT-11 (the record's glyph at its authored `home_attach` point, seam drawn while berthed and erased once absorbed) and its reference captures (AC-CT-120) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *What the player learns:* "a ship that is literally assembled from your history" (CON:200, Retention: Investment) is visible on the one surface that cannot lie about it.
120	
121	**Moment-ordering tripwire.** A 30-minute MVP solo session (CON:483-485) reaches Moments 1 and 2 almost certainly, Moment 4 if the weld is reached, Moment 3 at the second launch. If playtest notes call the chart "empty" or "useless" before Moment 1's tick appears, the cure is **not** to add data to the chart; it is to check that the residual lamp and the tick are legible (WM, ART). Adding a label, cost or name is never one of the levers.
122	
123	### Design tests
124	
125	> **Primary (P1):** "A chart that tells you where to go and what it costs vs. a chart that only remembers what your crew lit → the one that remembers."
126	> **Secondary (pause, P1 + P2):** "A pause that softens the world vs. a pause that holds the world exactly as it was → the held world."
127	> **Tertiary (records, P5 + the no-win-state anti-pillar):** "A save screen that shows how far you have come vs. a log line that shows where you were → the log line."
128	
129	| Test | Rejects | Checkable as |
130	|---|---|---|
131	| Primary | fuel cost, travel time, ETA, distance label, danger/loot rating, "recommended", a name on an UNSEEN node, an interpolated pod marker, a route reconstructed from the pick | review against WM:1036-1050 and CT-35; lint on strings (CT-28); (auto) the chart double reads only `web.view` and never `web.leg_timing()` (CT-27) |
132	| Secondary | dim, blur, desaturation, vignette, scrim, slow-motion, a calming cue, a sanity-relief effect, any element that changes with sanity stage | screenshots at stage 0 and forced stage 3 (AC-SN-83); pixel diff of the world region before Esc and while the panel is up equals zero |
133	| Tertiary | thumbnail, completion %, "rings charted", achievement row, wall-clock nudge, "you died", "game over" | screenshot of UI-4; SL vocabulary lint (SL AC-SL-86) |
134	
135	Further tests this system adds, from the concept's own form: a **dimmed or blurred world behind the pause panel vs the world frozen exactly as lit → frozen**; a **death screen, "loading" indicator or tip vs black then control (ART 2.10, SL UI-6) → black**; a **minimap in play vs a chart you open (ART 7.0 "No minimap in play") → the chart you open**; a **confirm dialog on the hop vs the console press as the point of no return (WM:1225) → the press**.
136	
137	### Under hallucination: how the fantasy deepens, never breaks
138	
139	The layer has **no corruptible surface** (CT-2; PIPE PR-3/PR-10; PF:223; SN:1226). "Deepens" therefore cannot mean "the menu lies". It means three things, and the third is this system's one new rule.
140	
141	1. **The contrast sharpens.** At stage 0 the panel and the world agree; at stage 3 the panel is the only thing on screen the player is sure of, and the world beside it is frozen mid-lie (Moment 2). The layer's value as an anchor rises exactly as the world's falls. Nothing on the layer changes for this to happen; the world changes around it. This is P4's "at least one channel of truth always remains", given a fixed place on screen (HR-6).
142	2. **The frozen lie is intended, and documented as intended.** `PAUSED_FROZEN` holds the last frame, including any hallucination, undimmed (PIPE:265). A tester or player at stage 3 will see a phantom held still beside a true menu. That image is the fantasy working, not a fault. It is an Edge Case and a QA note (Edge Cases, Acceptance Criteria), so nobody "fixes" it with a dim.
143	3. **Narrow truth (CT-39): the table is true, and it is not an oracle.** *The layer displays only facts that no hallucination class can lie about.* Every field it draws comes from `web.view`, `SaveInfo`, `save_status` or `restore_reason`, and none of them is touched by classes (a), (b), (c) or (d). Conversely, **a fact that any hallucination class can falsify (Graph state, entity presence or position, salvage contents or value, a crewmate's rendered form or location) never enters the layer**, because a true copy of it on a free, pausable menu would make that lie free to disprove, and P4 requires that "checking costs time, risk or trust" (CON:263). This is the positive form of the negative rules CT-31 to CT-37 and gives the review one test instead of seven lists: *if a hallucination could make the world disagree with this field, the field does not belong here.*
144	
145	| Hallucination class | May it touch the Chart Table? | Why the fantasy holds |
146	|---|---|---|
147	| (a) phantom entities | Never. No entity, threat, proximity or "last seen" element exists on the layer (CT-32; HE:377, :1358) | the chart cannot confirm or deny a phantom, so checking one still costs a look into the dark |
148	| (b) false system states | Never. No Graph, module or suit datum exists on the layer (CT-34, CT-37; LSG:22 "never operates the Graph as a menu") | the scrubber that reads fixed must still be checked against the frost |
149	| (c) crewmates as horrors (VS-B) | Never wraps the layer. **Risk K1:** ART 7.4 / 7.5 reserve a crewmate beam-shape glyph on the chart as "one of exactly three ways to find a crewmate". Under OVERLAY that glyph is a zero-cost check against class (c) | the human channel is P1-inviolable, so the glyph is true; whether its *price* is right is VS-B's call (Open Questions) |
150	| (d) phantom salvage | Never. No loot value, contents or remaining-salvage count (CT-33; BS:334, AC-BS-47c) | the crate is still checked by weight, a second scanner or the trip home (CON P4(d)) |
151	
152	**Negatives lifted into rules:** no gleam, glide, tremor or settle on any element (ART 7.3: those signatures are readings only); no violet or flesh at any stage (ART 4.6, HR-6); no change of filament drift, ring darkness, font, scale or layout with sanity stage; no sanity-stage-dependent audio on the UI bus (AA:562).
153	
154	### Tone and language
155	
156	**Register:** ship-log, low-affect, factual, few words (SL:127, SL:1008; WM:1319). The Chart Table speaks like a logbook kept by a tired, competent person. Final copy is UX's and the narrative director's (CT-28); this section fixes the register and the lexicon the copy must respect. Fixed item labels: Resume, Chart, Display & Comfort, Save & Quit (CT-3); Continue, New campaign, Quit (CT-23; SL:993).
157	
158	| Use | Never use (on any surface of this layer) | Why |
159	|---|---|---|
160	| chart, record, sortie, ring (as place, `RING <n>`), pod, home | map completion, explored, discovered %, charted %, progress | P5 / no win state (WM guard rail 5) |
161	| Continue, Save & Quit, New campaign, newest record, autosave | load game, slot, checkpoint, respawn, save point, quicksave, progress saved (SL:993; AC-SL-86) | SL vocabulary is locked |
162	| *(no word at all beside a node)* | destination, objective, quest, target recommended, danger, safe, threat, loot, value, reward, distance, ETA, fuel, cost, time | P1 / P3 / guard rail 1 |
163	| `IN TRANSIT` (instrument face, iff `pod_at == IN_FLIGHT`, CT-15) | arriving in, departing, % complete, any countdown | WM:300, WM:1048 |
164	| *(silence)* | you died, game over, lost, failed run, the web took you, sanity, attention, the web is watching | SL:993; P3; P4; no authored story |
165	
166	No exclamation marks, no emoji, no second-person exhortation ("Be careful out there"), no tips, no rhetorical questions (SL:127; no pause-time hint system). Sentences in messages state one fact each. Numbers appear only where Save/Load already supplies them (playtime, crew count) in the tabular instrument numerals (ART 7.1). *Illustrative register* (not final copy): acceptable, "Newest record unreadable. Continuing from the one before it." (SL UI-7 placeholder, SL:1003); rejected, "Oh no! Your save was corrupted, but don't worry, we found a backup!" (exclamation, affect, reassurance); rejected, a node line carrying a distance, a time and a fuel figure (every element is guard rail G6).
167	
168	### Reference techniques: adopt and reject
169	
170	| Reference | Technique | Verdict |
171	|---|---|---|
172	| *Project Zomboid* (designer touchstone) | a solo pause that freezes the world in place; a world map that records only what the character has seen | **Adopt** the plain freeze (solo, CT-4) and "the map shows what you saw" (WM-28). **Reject** player-drawn map annotations at MVP (a VS Codex question, CT-38) and any loot or zombie-density overlay |
173	| *Beyond the Aquila Rift* (concept inspiration) | the comforting false room the protagonist is kept in "for his own good" | **Reject, and invert.** The Chart Table is the anti-Aquila surface: it never offers the kind lie. No softened world behind the panel, no reassurance copy, no "everything is fine" summary. The kind lie belongs to Sanity's world filter, never to this layer |
174	| *Pandorum* (concept inspiration) | the crew's own light as the only reliable thing in a ship that lies about its state | **Adopt** the principle that the human thing is the trustworthy thing: the chart is drawn in human, rectilinear geometry over an inhuman shape (ART 3.4). Nothing visual from the film enters the layer |
175	| *FTL: Faster Than Light* | a node map with one click per jump; beacon hazard icons; the rebel-fleet advance line | **Adopt** the one-step pick on a small node graph. **Reject** hazard / distress / store icons, the fuel counter beside the map, and above all the **advancing fleet line** (a progress / threat datum on the map, G4 and G6) |
176	| *Sunless Sea* | a chart filled in only by sailing it; fog as default | **Adopt** "charted only by going and looking" (the Tungsten tick, Moment 1). **Reject** the Terror, fuel and supply counters beside its chart (P3: never a meter) |

content.content:
**PC-1. Three parts, and the control-manifest lines that separate them.** (a) The **Input Adapter** reads devices, quantises, and submits `PLAYER`-origin commands as peer 1 acting on the entity the binding table binds to PlayerId 1 (CR-7). It writes no block, ever; it owns only local state (raw aim, last-acknowledged intents, hold timers, run latch, active device, context, pre-play tokens). It samples input **in the physics callback immediately before `Kernel.step()`**, so an intent submitted in frame N is frozen into tick T's P1 batch, applied in P2 and integrated by Body in P3 of the same tick — one tick of latency, never two. It never requests a Sanity, Attention or `PERCEPTION_OUT` rea

**PC-2. Input model: contexts, actions, intents, commands.** The game reads **named actions** (`StringName`, rebindable), never raw keys and never `device == 0` (4.7: `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` / `DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD`; identify devices by event type). **→ ADR** (InputMap vs a custom binding layer; edge detection by event vs polling).

*Contexts.* Exactly one context is active: `gameplay`, `chart_table`, `inspect_card`, `chat`. Entering any non-`gameplay` context sends `set_move_intent {NONE}` and clears the run latch; entering `chart_table` or `chat` also submits `cancel_channel` for a hold- **or** toggle-mode channel (in the co-op overlay the sim keeps running and a channel the player cannot see must not keep burning); entering `inspect_card` does **not** cancel the channel, so the Pillar 4 "second instrument" check on the pipe being welded is free (the zeroed move intent is not a move, the channel continues, `interact` is still tracked for hold mode and a release inside the card still cancels; `cancel` closes the card f

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-CT-14 (auto half, L1780) vs Detailed Rules CT-45 (c) (L498), AC-CT-135 (c), AC-CT-14 half b and manual half, EC-CT-14
findings.finding: AC-CT-14 (auto, UI, BLOCKING) says: GIVEN POINTER{MOVE} over item X, then NAV_DOWN{DOWN}, THEN the retained focus id is the item BELOW the retained control. CT-45 (c) and AC-CT-135 (c) say the first NAV_DOWN or ACCEPT_DOWN after pointer motion ONLY reveals the bracket on the retained focus and 'moves nothing and activates nothing'. AC-CT-14's own half b and its manual half ('WHEN a pad direction is pressed, THEN the bracket reappears on the retained focus') follow the reveal-only rule, so the NAV case in the auto half contradicts the rest of the same criterion. A correct implementation of CT-45 (c) fails AC-CT-14 auto; an implementation that passes it makes the first NAV press act on an unseen bracket, which is exactly what (c) forbids. Same stale-AC pattern as the earlier passes (the reveal rule was added in the second re-review, the AC was only partly updated).
findings.fix: Rewrite the auto half: 'GIVEN POINTER{MOVE} over X (bracket hidden, focus retained on Y), WHEN the first NAV_DOWN{DOWN} arrives, THEN the bracket is shown on Y and the retained focus id is still Y; WHEN a second NAV_DOWN arrives, THEN the retained focus id is the item below Y (not below X).' Keep 'no ui_* action is used'. Then grep AC-CT-14, AC-CT-135, EC-CT-14 and CT-6 for 'reappears' and make all four say reveal-first.

findings.section: Detailed Rules CT-1 (L230), AC-CT-8 (L1772), Interactions row for Player Controller (L592, 'PCI:62 pause reachable from both') vs Player Controller PC-2 context table / context return table (PCI L101, L109, L116)
findings.finding: CT-1 says the layer is opened by chart_table 'from the gameplay or inspect_card context', and AC-CT-8 (auto, Logic, BLOCKING) asserts the layer opens in both. The Controller owns contexts and, in its 2026-10-27 re-review amendment, rules: in inspect_card, chart_table 'closes the card first (context return table), channel untouched, no pause on that press'; 'no pause and no overlay opens on that press'; 'So chart_table is never entered from inspect_card'. A correct Adapter fails AC-CT-8, and AC-CT-109's contract test keeps the Controller double honest, so the conflict surfaces at integration. CT-1 and AC-CT-8 carry no amendment marker acknowledging the change (CT-1 line has none). Owner wins (G1): the Controller's table stands and the Chart Table conforms.
findings.fix: CT-1: opened from the gameplay context only (and note PC-2: a press in inspect_card closes the card and does not open the layer or call request_pause; a second press, now in gameplay, opens it). AC-CT-8: GIVEN gameplay, chart_table opens the layer (PANEL, request_pause once in SOLO); GIVEN inspect_card, chart_table closes the card, the layer stays CLOSED and no kernel call is made; a second press opens it; GIVEN chat, it does not open. Update the Player Controller Interactions row (L592), CT-5 and the coverage matrix. Add *(Amended 2026-10-28 - cross-GDD fix, G1)* markers.

findings.section: Cross-References ASK-CT-15 (L1718), Detailed Rules CT-5/CT-45, Dependencies, ASK-CT-19 / D.2 / Tuning Knobs C-10, AC-CT-117/118/127/135 vs Player Controller GDD

findings.fix: Fix in player-controller-input.md under G6 (owner adds): publish the MenuInput stream (NAV down/up, ACCEPT down/up, BACK, CLOSE, FOCUS_OUT/IN, DEVICE_CHANGED, POINTER) with echo suppression, hysteresis, cardinal-axis rule and closing-control latch; drop LMB from the chart_table accept (PCI L118, L75 context note); cap the quit-without-saving hold base at HOLD_EFF_MAX_S - 0.4 s = 1.5 s or narrow the CONFIRM_HOLD_S range for the Delete-paired holds. Then mark ASK-CT-15/19 answered here. If the Controller edit is declined, add the stated fallback to ASK-CT-15 and scope C-10/AC-CT-127 to bases <= 1.5 s.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-CT-137 (L1929), CT-21 (L400), ASK-CT-18 (L1721), TX-39, OQ-CT-34/37, F-D vs Save/Load SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS (SL L962) and SL window-close edge cases (SL L838)
findings.finding: AC-CT-137 (auto, Logic, BLOCKING) requires FAILED within 3,000 ms and says a configured SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS above 3,000 ms is 'reported by the contract test (AC-CT-109) as a mismatch'. Save/Load (owner, G1) still defaults SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS to 5,000 ms and AC-SL-45c asserts the hold at 5,000 ms, so the contract test fails against the real owner. Separately, with a SaveDouble that 'never returns' nothing publishes save_status FAILED, so the 3,000 ms assertion tests the double's script, not the layer, unless the layer runs its own watchdog, which CT-21 forbids. TX-39 and OQ-CT-37 depend on a Save/Load 'window-close write in progress' signal that Save/Load does not publish (SL L838 publishes quit_held only after the timeout), and quit_held is listed in Dependencies (L1030) but no CT rule or TX row consumes it. The G2 ruling (ask for 3,000 ms) was recorded but its owner-side half was not applied.
findings.fix: Preferred: edit save-load-and-versioned-format.md (G6): SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS default 3,000 ms (range unchanged), AC-SL-45c at 3,000, and add a published 'quit_write_in_progress' read (or define it as save_status WRITING with kind QUIT) so TX-39 has a trigger; give quit_held a consumer row in the Chart Table (a held window close lands in SAVE_FAILED/UI3_PLATE). Rewrite AC-CT-137: 'GIVEN a SaveDouble scripted to publish save_status FAILED at the configured SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS, THEN FAILED is drawn on the next frame and nothing else is added; the contract test asserts the Save/Load default is <= 3,000 ms.' Alternative: conform to SL's 5,000 ms and delete the 3,000 ms ceiling from CT-21.

findings.section: Edge Cases EC-CT-70 (L1010) vs Save/Load SL-23 / ruling R13-R14 (restore_epoch)
findings.finding: EC-CT-70 says that Save & Quit, Continue or Quit without saving cannot reroll because 'every random stream is derived from the world seed and a counter held in state, so a reload reproduces rather than rerolls'. Under R13/R14 (Save/Load SL-23, AC-SL-142) only Continue of the newest QUIT generation carries the epoch; a death restore, and a Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation (which is what Quit without saving leaves), advance restore_epoch and change threat draws by design. The header (L15) says R13/R14 'do not touch this file', but this edge case states a determinism claim they falsify.
findings.fix: Reword EC-CT-70: Save & Quit then Continue carries the epoch and reproduces exactly; any other restore (death, Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation after Quit without saving or a crash) advances restore_epoch (Save/Load SL-23), so threat draws differ by design while physical state is restored exactly; the menu offers no seed field. Cite AC-SL-142.

findings.section: Formulas D.4 / CT-7 / CT-11 / EC-CT-4 / AC-CT-94 (HOME at a derelict)

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-CT-14 (auto half, L1780) vs Detailed Rules CT-45 (c) (L498), AC-CT-135 (c), AC-CT-14 half b and manual half, EC-CT-14
findings.finding: AC-CT-14 (auto, UI, BLOCKING) says: GIVEN POINTER{MOVE} over item X, then NAV_DOWN{DOWN}, THEN the retained focus id is the item BELOW the retained control. CT-45 (c) and AC-CT-135 (c) say the first NAV_DOWN or ACCEPT_DOWN after pointer motion ONLY reveals the bracket on the retained focus and 'moves nothing and activates nothing'. AC-CT-14's own half b and its manual half ('WHEN a pad direction is pressed, THEN the bracket reappears on the retained focus') follow the reveal-only rule, so the NAV case in the auto half contradicts the rest of the same criterion. A correct implementation of CT-45 (c) fails AC-CT-14 auto; an implementation that passes it makes the first NAV press act on an unseen bracket, which is exactly what (c) forbids. Same stale-AC pattern as the earlier passes (the reveal rule was added in the second re-review, the AC was only partly updated).
findings.fix: Rewrite the auto half: 'GIVEN POINTER{MOVE} over X (bracket hidden, focus retained on Y), WHEN the first NAV_DOWN{DOWN} arrives, THEN the bracket is shown on Y and the retained focus id is still Y; WHEN a second NAV_DOWN arrives, THEN the retained focus id is the item below Y (not below X).' Keep 'no ui_* action is used'. Then grep AC-CT-14, AC-CT-135, EC-CT-14 and CT-6 for 'reappears' and make all four say reveal-first.

CT-1 and AC-CT-8 carry no amendment marker acknowledging the change (CT-1 line has none). Owner wins (G1): the Controller's table stands and the Chart Table conforms.
findings.fix: CT-1: opened from the gameplay context only (and note PC-2: a press in inspect_card closes the card and does not open the layer or call request_pause; a second press, now in gameplay, opens it). AC-CT-8: GIVEN gameplay, chart_table opens the layer (PANEL, request_pause once in SOLO); GIVEN inspect_card, chart_table closes the card, the layer stays CLOSED and no kernel call is made; a second press opens it; GIVEN chat, it does not open. findings.section: Cross-References ASK-CT-15 (L1718), Detailed Rules CT-5/CT-45, Dependencies, ASK-CT-19 / D.2 / Tuning Knobs C-10, AC-CT-117/118/127/135 vs Player Controller GDD

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-CT-137 (L1929), CT-21 (L400), ASK-CT-18 (L1721), TX-39, OQ-CT-34/37, F-D vs Save/Load SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS (SL L962) and SL window-close edge cases (SL L838)
findings.finding: AC-CT-137 (auto, Logic, BLOCKING) requires FAILED within 3,000 ms and says a configured SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS above 3,000 ms is 'reported by the contract test (AC-CT-109) as a mismatch'. Save/Load (owner, G1) still defaults SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS to 5,000 ms and AC-SL-45c asserts the hold at 5,000 ms, so the contract test fails against the real owner. Separately, with a SaveDouble that 'never returns' nothing publishes save_status FAILED, so the 3,000 ms assertion tests the double's script, not the layer, unless the layer runs its own watchdog, which CT-21 forbids. TX-39 and OQ-CT-37 depend on a Save/Load 'window-close write in progress' signal that Save/Load does not publish (SL L838 publishes quit_held only after the timeout), and quit_held is listed in Dependencies (L1030) but no CT rule or TX row consumes it. findings.section: Edge Cases EC-CT-70 (L1010) vs Save/Load SL-23 / ruling R13-R14 (restore_epoch)
findings.finding: EC-CT-70 says that Save & Quit, Continue or Quit without saving cannot reroll because 'every random stream is derived from the world seed and a counter held in state, so a reload reproduces rather than rerolls'. Under R13/R14 (Save/Load SL-23, AC-SL-142) only Continue of the newest QUIT generation carries the epoch; a death restore, and a Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation (which is what Quit without saving leaves), advance restore_epoch and change threat draws by design. The header (L15) says R13/R14 'do not touch this file', but this edge case states a determinism claim they falsify.
findings.fix: Reword EC-CT-70: Save & Quit then Continue carries the epoch and reproduces exactly; any other restore (death, Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation after Quit without saving or a crash) advances restore_epoch (Save/Load SL-23), so threat draws differ by design while physical state is restored exactly; the menu offers no seed field. Cite AC-SL-142.

findings.section: Formulas D.4 / CT-7 / CT-11 / EC-CT-4 / AC-CT-94 (HOME at a derelict)
findings.finding: D.4 and AC-CT-21 put HOME_ID in legal_targets when the pod is at a derelict, i.e. HOME is 'selectable'; CT-11 says HOME is not selectable, EC-CT-4 and AC-CT-94 say accept on HOME changes nothing and ChartPick stays NONE, and CT-7 defines setting a pick only when pod_at == HOME_ID. The terms selectable, legal target and focusable are used interchangeably, so an implementer cannot tell whether accept on HOME at a derelict sets a pick (and whether CT-8 (3) then fires).

findings.fix: AC-CT-84: 'the bracket has covered >= 70 % of its travel at t = 50 ms and exactly 100 % at t = 100 ms, strictly monotone, no overshoot' (thresholds PLACEHOLDER, art-director owned). AC-CT-81: 'fails if the 95th percentile exceeds 0.5 ms [PLACEHOLDER] or P99 frame time exceeds 90 % of the RM-DESKTOP/RM-DECK ceiling'. AC-CT-37: 'the fill/interior luminance ratio is >= 3:1 by computed Y, and the needle protrudes >= 2 art px beyond each bar edge'. data.summary: Verdict: NEEDS REVISION (fourth pass, read-only, nothing edited). All three prior blockers are RESOLVED and verified against both this file and the siblings (D.4 / AC-CT-21 / EC-CT-9 agree; the queued-reopen cue is in CT-29, CT-VA-23, CT-GF-11, AC-CT-76 and AC-CT-138 and Adaptive Audio's AAV-40 / AC-AA-157; CT-4 and AC-CT-6 now match the idempotent CT-3). The ASK-CT-13/14 POD/DOCK split and pick_glyph_key echo are accepted by Interaction, Layout and Web Map, so berth-and-weld stays in MVP. All 8 sections are present, every designed dependency GDD exists, and the VS/Alpha dependencies are undesigned per R9. The arithmetic recomputes cleanly (D.1 to D.10 at the registry defaults, canvas rows, hold frames, drift steps 168/240/378/474/624/708/840 and the 599-step total, ring tones, draw-call counts). Five BLOCKING defects remain. Three are in this file: AC-CT-14's auto half contradicts CT-45 (c) and AC-CT-135 (c) (the first NAV press only reveals the bracket); CT-1 and AC-CT-8 say the layer opens from inspect_card although the Controller (owner, G1) now says chart_table in inspect_card only closes the card; and the glossary's WM-36 list omits leg_target_id and leg_dir, so AC-CT-4 fails a correct CT-15 implementation. Two are owner-side gaps the 2026-10-28 pass did not land under G6: the Controller still has no MenuInput feed, still lists LMB as accept, and its hold range makes C-10 / AC-CT-127 unsatisfiable above a 1.5 s base; and Save/Load still defaults SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS to 5,000 ms with no window-close-in-progress signal, so AC-CT-137 and TX-39 cannot pass. RECOMMENDED items: the missing '### D.2' heading (carried), a stale determinism claim in EC-CT-70 after R13/R14, the BACK-leg justification now false because WM-36 publishes leg_origin_id, stale F-B and coverage-matrix text, the open Pipeline hide-layer-2 ask behind AC-CT-45, HOME-at-a-derelict selectability wording, the REDUCED >= normal re-open constraint, the flipped UI-9 order in two places, and four untestable ACs with rewrites. No user ruling or delegated-ruling marker was reversed.
